   155→def _seed_plan_start_scores(plan: dict[str, object], state: state_mod.StateModel) -> bool:
   156→    """Set plan_start_scores when beginning a new queue cycle."""
   157→    if plan.get("plan_start_scores"):
   158→        return False
   159→    scores = state_mod.score_snapshot(state)
   160→    if scores.strict is None:
   161→        return False
   162→    plan["plan_start_scores"] = {
   163→        "strict": scores.strict,
   164→        "overall": scores.overall,
   165→        "objective": scores.objective,
   166→        "verified": scores.verified,
   167→    }
   168→    return True
   169→
   170→
   171→def _clear_plan_start_scores_if_queue_empty(
   172→    state: state_mod.StateModel, plan: dict[str, object]
   173→) -> bool:
   174→    """Clear plan-start score snapshot once the queue is fully drained."""
   175→    if not plan.get("plan_start_scores"):
   176→        return False
   177→
   178→    try:
   179→        from desloppify.app.commands.helpers.queue_progress import plan_aware_queue_count
   180→
   181→        queue_empty = plan_aware_queue_count(state, plan) == 0
   182→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   183→        logging.debug("Plan operation skipped: %s", exc)
   184→        return False
   185→    if not queue_empty:
   186→        return False
   187→    state["_plan_start_scores_for_reveal"] = dict(plan["plan_start_scores"])
   188→    plan["plan_start_scores"] = {}
   189→    return True

   191→
   192→def _reconcile_plan_post_scan(runtime: "ScanRuntime") -> None:
   193→    """Reconcile plan queue metadata and stale subjective review dimensions."""
   194→    try:
   195→        plan_path = runtime.state_path.parent / "plan.json" if runtime.state_path else None
   196→        plan = load_plan(plan_path)
   197→        dirty = False
   198→
   199→        if _apply_plan_reconciliation(plan, runtime.state, reconcile_plan_after_scan):
   200→            dirty = True
   201→
   202→        unscored_changed = _sync_unscored_dimensions(plan, runtime.state, sync_unscored_dimensions)
   203→        if unscored_changed:
   204→            dirty = True
   205→            append_log_entry(plan, "sync_unscored", actor="system",
   206→                             detail={"changes": True})
   207→
   208→        stale_changed = _sync_stale_dimensions(plan, runtime.state, sync_stale_dimensions)
   209→        if stale_changed:
   210→            dirty = True
   211→            append_log_entry(plan, "sync_stale", actor="system",
   212→                             detail={"changes": True})
   213→
   214→        from desloppify.app.commands.helpers.score import target_strict_score_from_config
   215→        _target_strict = target_strict_score_from_config(runtime.config, fallback=95.0)
   216→
   217→        auto_changed = _sync_auto_clusters(
   218→            plan, runtime.state, target_strict=_target_strict,
   219→        )
   220→        if auto_changed:
   221→            dirty = True
   222→            append_log_entry(plan, "auto_cluster", actor="system",
   223→                             detail={"changes": True})
   224→
   225→        triage_sync = sync_triage_needed(plan, runtime.state)
   226→        if triage_sync.changes:
   227→            dirty = True
   228→            if triage_sync.injected:
   229→                print(
   230→                    colorize(
   231→                        "  Plan: planning mode needed — review findings changed since last triage.",
   232→                        "cyan",
   233→                    )
   234→                )
   235→                append_log_entry(plan, "sync_triage", actor="system",
   236→                                 detail={"injected": True})
   237→
   238→        create_plan_sync = sync_create_plan_needed(plan, runtime.state)
   239→        if create_plan_sync.changes:
   240→            dirty = True
   241→            if create_plan_sync.injected:
   242→                print(
   243→                    colorize(
   244→                        "  Plan: reviews complete — `workflow::create-plan` queued.",
   245→                        "cyan",
   246→                    )
   247→                )
   248→                append_log_entry(plan, "sync_create_plan", actor="system",
   249→                                 detail={"injected": True})
   250→
   251→        seeded = _seed_plan_start_scores(plan, runtime.state)
   252→        if seeded:
   253→            dirty = True
   254→            append_log_entry(plan, "seed_start_scores", actor="system",
   255→                             detail={})
   256→        # Only clear scores that existed before this reconcile pass —
   257→        # never clear scores we just seeded in the same scan.
   258→        if not seeded and _clear_plan_start_scores_if_queue_empty(runtime.state, plan):
   259→            dirty = True
   260→            append_log_entry(plan, "clear_start_scores", actor="system",
   261→                             detail={})
   262→
   263→        if dirty:
   264→            save_plan(plan, plan_path)
   265→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   266→        logging.debug("Plan operation skipped: %s", exc)
   267→

   269→def _state_subjective_assessments(
   270→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   271→) -> dict[str, object]:
   272→    """Return normalized subjective assessment store from state."""
   273→    assessments = state.get("subjective_assessments")
   274→    if isinstance(assessments, dict):
   275→        return assessments
   276→    raise ScanStateContractError(
   277→        "state.subjective_assessments must be an object; rerun with a valid state file"
   278→    )

   281→def _state_lang_capabilities(
   282→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   283→) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   284→    """Return normalized language capability map from state."""
   285→    capabilities = state.get("lang_capabilities")
   286→    if capabilities is None:
   287→        normalized: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
   288→        state["lang_capabilities"] = normalized
   289→        return normalized
   290→    if isinstance(capabilities, dict):
   291→        return capabilities
   292→    raise ScanStateContractError(
   293→        "state.lang_capabilities must be an object when present"
   294→    )

   297→def _state_findings(state: state_mod.StateModel) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
   298→    """Return normalized finding map from state."""
   299→    findings = state.get("findings")
   300→    if isinstance(findings, dict):
   301→        return findings
   302→    raise ScanStateContractError(
   303→        "state.findings must be an object; state file appears corrupted"
   304→    )

   354→def _configure_lang_runtime(
   355→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   356→    config: dict[str, object],
   357→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   358→    lang: LangRun | None,
   359→) -> LangRun | None:
   360→    """Populate runtime context and threshold overrides for a selected language."""
   361→    if not lang:
   362→        return None
   363→
   364→    lang_options = resolve_lang_runtime_options(args, lang)
   365→    lang_settings = resolve_lang_settings(config, lang)
   366→    runtime_lang = make_lang_run(
   367→        lang,
   368→        overrides=LangRunOverrides(
   369→            review_cache=state.get("review_cache", {}),
   370→            review_max_age_days=config.get("review_max_age_days", 30),
   371→            runtime_settings=lang_settings,
   372→            runtime_options=lang_options,
   373→            large_threshold_override=config.get("large_files_threshold", 0),
   374→            props_threshold_override=config.get("props_threshold", 0),
   375→        ),
   376→    )
   377→
   378→    lang_capabilities = _state_lang_capabilities(state)
   379→    lang_capabilities[runtime_lang.name] = {
   380→        "fixers": sorted(runtime_lang.fixers.keys()),
   381→        "typecheck_cmd": runtime_lang.typecheck_cmd,
   382→    }
   383→    return runtime_lang
   384→
   385→
   386→def _reset_subjective_assessments_for_scan_reset(
   387→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   388→    *,
   389→    lang_name: str | None = None,
   390→) -> int:
   391→    """Reset known subjective dimensions to 0 so the next scan starts fresh."""
   392→    assessments = _state_subjective_assessments(state)
   393→
   394→    reset_keys = {
   395→        key.strip()
   396→        for key in assessments
   397→        if isinstance(key, str) and key.strip()
   398→    }
   399→    reset_keys.update(_subjective_reset_dimensions(lang_name=lang_name))
   400→
   401→    now = state_mod.utc_now()
   402→    for key in sorted(reset_keys):
   403→        payload = assessments.get(key)
   404→        if isinstance(payload, dict):
   405→            payload["score"] = 0.0
   406→            payload["source"] = "scan_reset_subjective"
   407→            payload["assessed_at"] = now
   408→            payload["reset_by"] = "scan_reset_subjective"
   409→            payload["placeholder"] = True
   410→            payload.pop("integrity_penalty", None)
   411→            payload.pop("components", None)
   412→            payload.pop("component_scores", None)
   413→            continue
   414→        assessments[key] = {
   415→            "score": 0.0,
   416→            "source": "scan_reset_subjective",
   417→            "assessed_at": now,
   418→            "reset_by": "scan_reset_subjective",
   419→            "placeholder": True,
   420→        }
   421→    return len(reset_keys)
   422→
   423→
   424→def _expire_provisional_manual_override_assessments(
   425→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   426→) -> int:
   427→    """Expire provisional manual-override assessments at scan start."""
   428→    assessments = _state_subjective_assessments(state)
   429→
   430→    now = state_mod.utc_now()
   431→    expired = 0
   432→    for payload in assessments.values():
   433→        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
   434→            continue
   435→        if payload.get("provisional_override") is not True:
   436→            continue
   437→        payload["score"] = 0.0
   438→        payload["source"] = "manual_override_expired"
   439→        payload["assessed_at"] = now
   440→        payload["reset_by"] = "manual_override_expired"
   441→        payload["placeholder"] = True
   442→        payload.pop("provisional_override", None)
   443→        payload.pop("provisional_until_scan", None)
   444→        payload.pop("integrity_penalty", None)
   445→        payload.pop("components", None)
   446→        payload.pop("component_scores", None)
   447→        expired += 1
   448→    return expired
   449→

   451→def prepare_scan_runtime(args) -> ScanRuntime:
   452→    """Resolve state/config/language and apply scan-time runtime settings."""
   453→    runtime = command_runtime(args)
   454→    state_file = runtime.state_path
   455→    state = runtime.state if isinstance(runtime.state, dict) else {}
   456→    state_mod.ensure_state_defaults(state)
   457→    path = Path(args.path)
   458→    config = runtime.config if isinstance(runtime.config, dict) else {}
   459→    lang_config = resolve_lang(args)
   460→    reset_subjective_count = 0
   461→    expired_manual_override_count = _expire_provisional_manual_override_assessments(
   462→        state
   463→    )
   464→    if getattr(args, "reset_subjective", False):
   465→        reset_subjective_count = _reset_subjective_assessments_for_scan_reset(
   466→            state,
   467→            lang_name=getattr(lang_config, "name", None),
   468→        )
   469→
   470→    include_slow = not getattr(args, "skip_slow", False)
   471→    profile = _resolve_scan_profile(getattr(args, "profile", None), lang_config)
   472→    effective_include_slow = _effective_include_slow(include_slow, profile)
   473→
   474→    lang = _configure_lang_runtime(args, config, state, lang_config)
   475→    coverage_warnings = _seed_runtime_coverage_warnings(lang)
   476→    zone_overrides_raw = config.get("zone_overrides")
   477→    zone_overrides = zone_overrides_raw if isinstance(zone_overrides_raw, dict) else None
   478→
   479→    return ScanRuntime(
   480→        args=args,
   481→        state_path=state_file,
   482→        state=state,
   483→        path=path,
   484→        config=config,
   485→        lang=lang,
   486→        lang_label=f" ({lang.name})" if lang else "",
   487→        profile=profile,
   488→        effective_include_slow=effective_include_slow,
   489→        zone_overrides=zone_overrides,
   490→        reset_subjective_count=reset_subjective_count,
   491→        expired_manual_override_count=expired_manual_override_count,
   492→        coverage_warnings=coverage_warnings,
   493→    )
   494→

   496→def _augment_with_stale_exclusion_findings(
   497→    findings: list[dict[str, Any]],
   498→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   499→) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   500→    """Append stale exclude findings when excluded dirs are unreferenced."""
   501→    extra_exclusions = get_exclusions()
   502→    if not (extra_exclusions and runtime.lang and runtime.lang.file_finder):
   503→        return findings
   504→
   505→    scanned_files = runtime.lang.file_finder(runtime.path)
   506→    stale = _audit_excluded_dirs(
   507→        extra_exclusions, scanned_files, PROJECT_ROOT
   508→    )
   509→    if not stale:
   510→        return findings
   511→
   512→    augmented = list(findings)
   513→    augmented.extend(stale)
   514→    for stale_finding in stale:
   515→        print(colorize(f"  ℹ {stale_finding['summary']}", "dim"))
   516→    return augmented
   517→
   518→
   519→def _augment_with_stale_wontfix_findings(
   520→    findings: list[dict[str, Any]],
   521→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   522→    *,
   523→    decay_scans: int,
   524→) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], int]:
   525→    """Append re-triage findings for stale/worsening wontfix debt."""
   526→    return _augment_stale_wontfix_impl(
   527→        findings,
   528→        state=runtime.state,
   529→        scan_path=runtime.path,
   530→        project_root=PROJECT_ROOT,
   531→        decay_scans=decay_scans,
   532→    )

   534→
   535→def run_scan_generation(
   536→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   537→) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], dict[str, object], dict[str, object] | None]:
   538→    """Run detector pipeline and return findings, potentials, and codebase metrics."""
   539→    enable_file_cache()
   540→    enable_parse_cache()
   541→    try:
   542→        findings, potentials = plan_mod.generate_findings(
   543→            runtime.path,
   544→            lang=runtime.lang,
   545→            options=PlanScanOptions(
   546→                include_slow=runtime.effective_include_slow,
   547→                zone_overrides=runtime.zone_overrides,
   548→                profile=runtime.profile,
   549→            ),
   550→        )
   551→    finally:
   552→        disable_parse_cache()
   553→        disable_file_cache()
   554→
   555→    codebase_metrics = _collect_codebase_metrics(runtime.lang, runtime.path)
   556→    _warn_explicit_lang_with_no_files(
   557→        runtime.args, runtime.lang, runtime.path, codebase_metrics
   558→    )
   559→    findings = _augment_with_stale_exclusion_findings(findings, runtime)
   560→    decay_scans = _coerce_int(
   561→        runtime.config.get("wontfix_decay_scans"),
   562→        default=_WONTFIX_DECAY_SCANS_DEFAULT,
   563→    )
   564→    findings, monitored_wontfix = _augment_with_stale_wontfix_findings(
   565→        findings,
   566→        runtime,
   567→        decay_scans=max(decay_scans, 0),
   568→    )
   569→    potentials["stale_wontfix"] = monitored_wontfix
   570→    return findings, potentials, codebase_metrics
   571→
   572→
   573→def merge_scan_results(
   574→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   575→    findings: list[dict[str, Any]],
   576→    potentials: dict[str, object],
   577→    codebase_metrics: dict[str, object] | None,
   578→) -> ScanMergeResult:
   579→    """Merge findings into persistent state and return diff + previous score snapshot."""
   580→    scan_path_rel = rel(str(runtime.path))
   581→    prev_scan_path = runtime.state.get("scan_path")
   582→    path_changed = prev_scan_path is not None and prev_scan_path != scan_path_rel
   583→
   584→    if not path_changed:
   585→        prev = state_mod.score_snapshot(runtime.state)
   586→    else:
   587→        prev = state_mod.ScoreSnapshot(None, None, None, None)
   588→    prev_dim_scores = (
   589→        runtime.state.get("dimension_scores", {}) if not path_changed else {}
   590→    )
   591→
   592→    if runtime.lang and runtime.lang.zone_map is not None:
   593→        runtime.state["zone_distribution"] = runtime.lang.zone_map.counts()
   594→    _persist_scan_coverage(runtime.state, runtime.lang)
   595→
   596→    target_score = target_strict_score_from_config(runtime.config, fallback=95.0)
   597→
   598→    diff = state_mod.merge_scan(
   599→        runtime.state,
   600→        findings,
   601→        options=state_mod.MergeScanOptions(
   602→            lang=runtime.lang.name if runtime.lang else None,
   603→            scan_path=scan_path_rel,
   604→            force_resolve=getattr(runtime.args, "force_resolve", False),
   605→            exclude=get_exclusions(),
   606→            potentials=potentials,
   607→            codebase_metrics=codebase_metrics,
   608→            include_slow=runtime.effective_include_slow,
   609→            ignore=runtime.config.get("ignore", []),
   610→            subjective_integrity_target=target_score,
   611→        ),
   612→    )
   613→
   614→    issues_mod.expire_stale_holistic(
   615→        runtime.state, runtime.config.get("holistic_max_age_days", 30)
   616→    )
   617→    state_mod.save_state(
   618→        runtime.state,
   619→        runtime.state_path,
   620→        subjective_integrity_target=target_score,
   621→    )
   622→
   623→    _clear_needs_rescan_flag(runtime.config)
   624→    _reconcile_plan_post_scan(runtime)
   625→
   626→    return ScanMergeResult(
   627→        diff=diff,
   628→        prev_overall=prev.overall,
   629→        prev_objective=prev.objective,
   630→        prev_strict=prev.strict,
   631→        prev_verified=prev.verified,
   632→        prev_dim_scores=prev_dim_scores,
   633→    )
   634→
   635→
   636→def resolve_noise_snapshot(
   637→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   638→    config: dict[str, object],
   639→) -> ScanNoiseSnapshot:
   640→    """Resolve noise budget settings and hidden finding counters."""
   641→    noise_budget, global_noise_budget, budget_warning = (
   642→        state_mod.resolve_finding_noise_settings(config)
   643→    )
   644→    findings_by_id = _state_findings(state)
   645→    open_findings = [
   646→        finding
   647→        for finding in state_mod.path_scoped_findings(
   648→            findings_by_id, state.get("scan_path")
   649→        ).values()
   650→        if finding.get("status") == "open"
   651→    ]
   652→    _, hidden_by_detector = state_mod.apply_finding_noise_budget(
   653→        open_findings,
   654→        budget=noise_budget,
   655→        global_budget=global_noise_budget,
   656→    )
   657→
   658→    return ScanNoiseSnapshot(
   659→        noise_budget=noise_budget,
   660→        global_noise_budget=global_noise_budget,
   661→        budget_warning=budget_warning,
   662→        hidden_by_detector=hidden_by_detector,
   663→        hidden_total=sum(hidden_by_detector.values()),
   664→    )
   665→
   666→
   667→def persist_reminder_history(
   668→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   669→    narrative: dict[str, object],
   670→) -> None:
   671→    """Persist reminder history emitted by narrative computation."""
   672→    if not (narrative and "reminder_history" in narrative):
   673→        return
   674→
   675→    runtime.state["reminder_history"] = narrative["reminder_history"]
   676→    target_score = target_strict_score_from_config(runtime.config, fallback=95.0)
   677→    state_mod.save_state(
   678→        runtime.state,
   679→        runtime.state_path,
   680→        subjective_integrity_target=target_score,
   681→    )
   682→
   683→
   684→__all__ = [
   685→    "ScanStateContractError",
   686→    "ScanMergeResult",

   691→    "prepare_scan_runtime",

   694→]

    31→def append_log_entry(
    32→    plan: PlanModel,
    33→    action: str,

    62→def _remove_id_from_lists(plan: PlanModel, finding_id: str) -> None:
    63→    """Remove a finding ID from queue_order and skipped."""
    64→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
    65→    skipped: dict[str, SkipEntry] = plan.get("skipped", {})
    66→    if finding_id in order:
    67→        order.remove(finding_id)
    68→    skipped.pop(finding_id, None)

    70→
    71→def _resolve_position(
    72→    order: list[str],
    73→    position: str,
    74→    target: str | None = None,
    75→    offset: int | None = None,
    76→    finding_ids: list[str] | None = None,
    77→) -> int:
    78→    """Resolve a position specifier to an insertion index.
    79→
    80→    *finding_ids* are the IDs being moved — used to calculate relative
    81→    positions when they already exist in the list.
    82→    """
    83→    moving = set(finding_ids or [])
    84→
    85→    if position == "top":
    86→        return 0
    87→    if position == "bottom":
    88→        return len(order)
    89→
    90→    if position in {"before", "after"} and target:
    91→        return _resolve_relative_position(order, moving, position=position, target=target)
    92→
    93→    if position in {"up", "down"} and offset is not None:
    94→        return _resolve_offset_position(
    95→            order,
    96→            moving,
    97→            position=position,
    98→            offset=offset,
    99→            finding_ids=finding_ids,
   100→        )
   101→
   102→    return len(order)
   103→
   104→
   105→def _resolve_relative_position(
   106→    order: list[str],
   107→    moving: set[str],
   108→    *,
   109→    position: str,
   110→    target: str,
   111→) -> int:
   112→    for i, item_id in enumerate(order):
   113→        if item_id == target and item_id not in moving:
   114→            return i if position == "before" else i + 1
   115→    return 0 if position == "before" else len(order)
   116→
   117→
   118→def _find_index(items: list[str], target: str) -> int | None:
   119→    for i, item_id in enumerate(items):
   120→        if item_id == target:
   121→            return i
   122→    return None
   123→
   124→
   125→def _resolve_offset_position(
   126→    order: list[str],
   127→    moving: set[str],
   128→    *,
   129→    position: str,
   130→    offset: int,
   131→    finding_ids: list[str] | None,
   132→) -> int:
   133→    if not finding_ids:
   134→        return 0 if position == "up" else len(order)
   135→    first_id = finding_ids[0]
   136→    clean_order = [x for x in order if x not in moving]
   137→    current_idx = _find_index(clean_order, first_id)
   138→    if current_idx is None:
   139→        if position == "up":
   140→            return max(0, len(clean_order) - offset)
   141→        return len(clean_order)
   142→    if position == "up":
   143→        return max(0, current_idx - offset)
   144→    return min(len(clean_order), current_idx + offset)
   145→
   146→
   147→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   148→# Move items
   149→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   150→
   151→def move_items(
   152→    plan: PlanModel,
   153→    finding_ids: list[str],
   154→    position: str,
   155→    target: str | None = None,
   156→    offset: int | None = None,
   157→) -> int:
   158→    """Move finding IDs to a position in queue_order. Returns count moved."""
   159→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   160→
   161→    # Triage stage IDs are workflow-managed and cannot be manually reordered
   162→    from desloppify.engine._plan.stale_dimensions import TRIAGE_IDS
   163→    finding_ids = [fid for fid in finding_ids if fid not in TRIAGE_IDS]
   164→    if not finding_ids:
   165→        return 0
   166→
   167→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   168→
   169→    # Remove from skipped if present
   170→    skipped: dict[str, SkipEntry] = plan.get("skipped", {})
   171→    for fid in finding_ids:
   172→        skipped.pop(fid, None)
   173→
   174→    # Remove from current position in order
   175→    for fid in finding_ids:
   176→        if fid in order:
   177→            order.remove(fid)
   178→
   179→    # Resolve insertion point
   180→    idx = _resolve_position(order, position, target, offset, finding_ids)
   181→
   182→    # Insert in original order
   183→    for i, fid in enumerate(finding_ids):
   184→        order.insert(idx + i, fid)
   185→
   186→    # Track user-promoted IDs only when explicitly moved to the front.
   187→    # Moving to bottom/down/after should not create a promotion barrier.
   188→    if position == "top":
   189→        promoted: list[str] = plan.get("promoted_ids", [])
   190→        existing_promoted = set(promoted)
   191→        for fid in finding_ids:
   192→            if fid not in existing_promoted:
   193→                promoted.append(fid)
   194→                existing_promoted.add(fid)
   195→        plan["promoted_ids"] = promoted
   196→
   197→    return len(finding_ids)

   203→
   204→def skip_items(
   205→    plan: PlanModel,
   206→    finding_ids: list[str],
   207→    *,
   208→    kind: str = "temporary",
   209→    reason: str | None = None,
   210→    note: str | None = None,
   211→    attestation: str | None = None,
   212→    review_after: int | None = None,
   213→    scan_count: int = 0,
   214→) -> int:
   215→    """Move finding IDs to the skipped dict. Returns count skipped."""
   216→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   217→    now = utc_now()
   218→    count = 0
   219→    skipped: dict[str, SkipEntry] = plan["skipped"]
   220→    skip_set = set(finding_ids)
   221→    promoted: list[str] = plan.get("promoted_ids", [])
   222→    plan["promoted_ids"] = [p for p in promoted if p not in skip_set]
   223→    for fid in finding_ids:
   224→        _remove_id_from_lists(plan, fid)
   225→        skipped[fid] = {
   226→            "finding_id": fid,
   227→            "kind": kind,
   228→            "reason": reason,
   229→            "note": note,
   230→            "attestation": attestation,
   231→            "created_at": now,
   232→            "review_after": review_after,
   233→            "skipped_at_scan": scan_count,
   234→        }
   235→        count += 1
   236→    return count
   237→
   238→
   239→def unskip_items(
   240→    plan: PlanModel, finding_ids: list[str]
   241→) -> tuple[int, list[str]]:
   242→    """Bring finding IDs back from skipped to the end of queue_order.
   243→
   244→    Returns ``(count_unskipped, permanent_ids_needing_state_reopen)``
   245→    where the second list contains IDs that were permanent or false_positive
   246→    and need their state-layer status reopened by the caller.
   247→    """
   248→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   249→    count = 0
   250→    need_reopen: list[str] = []
   251→    skipped: dict[str, SkipEntry] = plan["skipped"]
   252→    for fid in finding_ids:
   253→        entry = skipped.pop(fid, None)
   254→        if entry is not None:
   255→            if entry.get("kind") in ("permanent", "false_positive"):
   256→                need_reopen.append(fid)
   257→            if fid not in plan["queue_order"]:
   258→                plan["queue_order"].append(fid)
   259→            count += 1
   260→    return count, need_reopen
   261→

   263→def resurface_stale_skips(
   264→    plan: PlanModel, current_scan_count: int
   265→) -> list[str]:
   266→    """Move temporary skips past their review_after threshold back to queue.
   267→
   268→    Returns list of resurfaced finding IDs.
   269→    """
   270→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   271→    skipped: dict[str, SkipEntry] = plan["skipped"]
   272→    resurfaced: list[str] = []
   273→    for fid in list(skipped):
   274→        entry = skipped[fid]
   275→        if entry.get("kind") != "temporary":
   276→            continue
   277→        review_after = entry.get("review_after")
   278→        if review_after is None:
   279→            continue
   280→        skipped_at = entry.get("skipped_at_scan", 0)
   281→        if current_scan_count >= skipped_at + review_after:
   282→            skipped.pop(fid)
   283→            if fid not in plan["queue_order"]:
   284→                plan["queue_order"].append(fid)
   285→            resurfaced.append(fid)
   286→    return resurfaced

   323→def create_cluster(
   324→    plan: PlanModel,
   325→    name: str,
   326→    description: str | None = None,
   327→    action: str | None = None,
   328→) -> Cluster:
   329→    """Create a named cluster. Raises ValueError if it already exists."""
   330→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   331→    if name.startswith("auto/"):
   332→        raise ValueError(
   333→            f"Cluster names starting with 'auto/' are reserved for auto-clusters: {name!r}"
   334→        )
   335→    if name.startswith("epic/"):
   336→        raise ValueError(
   337→            f"Cluster names starting with 'epic/' are reserved for triage epics: {name!r}"
   338→        )
   339→    if name in plan["clusters"]:

   341→    now = utc_now()
   342→    cluster: Cluster = {

   349→        "cluster_key": "",
   350→        "action": action,

   357→def add_to_cluster(
   358→    plan: PlanModel, cluster_name: str, finding_ids: list[str]
   359→) -> int:
   360→    """Add finding IDs to a cluster. Returns count added."""
   361→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   362→    cluster = plan["clusters"].get(cluster_name)
   363→    if cluster is None:
   364→        raise ValueError(f"Cluster {cluster_name!r} does not exist")
   365→
   366→    member_ids: list[str] = cluster["finding_ids"]
   367→    count = 0
   368→    now = utc_now()
   369→    for fid in finding_ids:

   373→        # Update override to track cluster membership
   374→        overrides = plan["overrides"]

   377→        overrides[fid]["cluster"] = cluster_name

   380→    cluster["updated_at"] = now

   384→def remove_from_cluster(
   385→    plan: PlanModel, cluster_name: str, finding_ids: list[str]

   388→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)

   390→    if cluster is None:

   392→
   393→    member_ids: list[str] = cluster["finding_ids"]
   394→    now = utc_now()
   395→    count = 0
   396→    for fid in finding_ids:
   397→        if fid in member_ids:
   398→            member_ids.remove(fid)

   400→        # Clear cluster from override
   401→        override = plan["overrides"].get(fid)
   402→        if override and override.get("cluster") == cluster_name:
   403→            override["cluster"] = None

   405→
   406→    # Mark auto-clusters as user_modified when items are manually removed
   407→    if count > 0 and cluster.get("auto"):

   410→    cluster["updated_at"] = now

   414→def delete_cluster(plan: PlanModel, name: str) -> list[str]:
   415→    """Delete a cluster and clear cluster refs from overrides. Returns orphaned IDs."""
   416→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   417→    cluster = plan["clusters"].pop(name, None)
   418→    if cluster is None:
   419→        raise ValueError(f"Cluster {name!r} does not exist")
   420→
   421→    orphaned = list(cluster.get("finding_ids", []))
   422→    now = utc_now()
   423→    for fid in orphaned:
   424→        override = plan["overrides"].get(fid)
   425→        if override and override.get("cluster") == name:
   426→            override["cluster"] = None
   427→            override["updated_at"] = now
   428→
   429→    if plan.get("active_cluster") == name:
   430→        plan["active_cluster"] = None
   431→
   432→    return orphaned

   435→def merge_clusters(
   436→    plan: PlanModel, source_name: str, target_name: str
   437→) -> tuple[int, list[str]]:
   438→    """Move all source findings to target, copy missing metadata, delete source.
   439→
   440→    Returns ``(added_count, source_finding_ids)``.
   441→    """
   442→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   443→    if source_name == target_name:
   444→        raise ValueError("Cannot merge a cluster into itself")
   445→    source = plan["clusters"].get(source_name)
   446→    if source is None:
   447→        raise ValueError(f"Source cluster {source_name!r} does not exist")
   448→    target = plan["clusters"].get(target_name)
   449→    if target is None:
   450→        raise ValueError(f"Target cluster {target_name!r} does not exist")
   451→
   452→    source_ids = list(source.get("finding_ids", []))
   453→    target_ids: list[str] = target["finding_ids"]
   454→    now = utc_now()
   455→
   456→    # Add source findings to target (deduplicate)
   457→    existing = set(target_ids)
   458→    added = 0
   459→    for fid in source_ids:
   460→        if fid not in existing:
   461→            target_ids.append(fid)
   462→            existing.add(fid)
   463→            added += 1
   464→        # Update override to point to target cluster
   465→        overrides = plan["overrides"]
   466→        if fid not in overrides:
   467→            overrides[fid] = {"finding_id": fid, "created_at": now}
   468→        overrides[fid]["cluster"] = target_name
   469→        overrides[fid]["updated_at"] = now
   470→
   471→    # Copy metadata from source if target is missing them
   472→    if not target.get("description") and source.get("description"):
   473→        target["description"] = source["description"]
   474→    if not target.get("action_steps") and source.get("action_steps"):
   475→        target["action_steps"] = list(source["action_steps"])
   476→    if not target.get("action") and source.get("action"):
   477→        target["action"] = source["action"]
   478→
   479→    target["updated_at"] = now
   480→
   481→    # Delete source cluster
   482→    plan["clusters"].pop(source_name, None)
   483→    if plan.get("active_cluster") == source_name:
   484→        plan["active_cluster"] = None
   485→
   486→    return added, source_ids
   487→

   489→def move_cluster(
   490→    plan: PlanModel,
   491→    cluster_name: str,
   492→    position: str,
   493→    target: str | None = None,
   494→    offset: int | None = None,
   495→) -> int:
   496→    """Move all cluster members as a contiguous block. Returns count moved."""
   497→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   498→    cluster = plan["clusters"].get(cluster_name)
   499→    if cluster is None:
   500→        raise ValueError(f"Cluster {cluster_name!r} does not exist")
   501→
   502→    member_ids = list(cluster.get("finding_ids", []))
   503→    if not member_ids:
   504→        return 0
   505→
   506→    return move_items(plan, member_ids, position, target, offset)

   513→def set_focus(plan: PlanModel, cluster_name: str) -> None:
   514→    """Set the active cluster focus."""
   515→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   516→    if cluster_name not in plan["clusters"]:
   517→        raise ValueError(f"Cluster {cluster_name!r} does not exist")
   518→    plan["active_cluster"] = cluster_name
   519→
   520→
   521→def clear_focus(plan: PlanModel) -> None:
   522→    """Clear the active cluster focus."""
   523→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   524→    plan["active_cluster"] = None
   525→
   526→
   527→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   528→# Reset
   529→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   530→
   531→def reset_plan(plan: PlanModel) -> None:
   532→    """Reset plan to empty state, preserving version and created timestamp."""
   533→    created = plan.get("created", utc_now())
   534→    plan.clear()
   535→    for k, v in empty_plan().items():
   536→        plan[k] = v
   537→    plan["created"] = created
   538→
   539→
   540→def purge_ids(plan: PlanModel, finding_ids: list[str]) -> int:
   541→    """Remove finding IDs from the plan entirely.
   542→
   543→    Cleans queue_order, skipped, and all cluster memberships.
   544→    Does NOT touch overrides (descriptions/notes are kept for history).
   545→    Returns count of IDs that were actually present somewhere.
   546→    """
   547→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   548→    found = 0
   549→
   550→    purge_set = set(finding_ids)
   551→    promoted: list[str] = plan.get("promoted_ids", [])
   552→    plan["promoted_ids"] = [p for p in promoted if p not in purge_set]
   553→
   554→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   555→    skipped: dict[str, SkipEntry] = plan["skipped"]
   556→    for fid in finding_ids:
   557→        was_present = False
   558→        if fid in order:
   559→            order.remove(fid)
   560→            was_present = True
   561→        if fid in skipped:
   562→            skipped.pop(fid)
   563→            was_present = True
   564→        for cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).values():
   565→            ids = cluster.get("finding_ids", [])
   566→            if fid in ids:
   567→                ids.remove(fid)
   568→                was_present = True
   569→        # Clear stale cluster reference from override (preserve notes/descriptions)
   570→        override = plan.get("overrides", {}).get(fid)
   571→        if override and override.get("cluster"):
   572→            override["cluster"] = None
   573→            override["updated_at"] = utc_now()
   574→        if was_present:
   575→            found += 1
   576→
   577→    return found
   578→

    24→def coerce_assessment_score(value: object) -> float | None:
    25→    """Normalize a subjective assessment score payload to a 0-100 float.
    26→
    27→    Returns ``None`` when the value cannot be interpreted as a numeric score
    28→    (e.g. bools, non-numeric strings, missing keys).
    29→    """
    30→    if is_numeric(value):
    31→        return round(max(0.0, min(100.0, float(value))), 1)
    32→    if isinstance(value, dict):
    33→        raw = value.get("score")
    34→        if not is_numeric(raw):
    35→            return None
    36→        return round(max(0.0, min(100.0, float(raw))), 1)
    37→    return None
    38→

    40→def _mark_stale_assessments_on_review_resolve(
    41→    state: StateModel,
    42→    *,
    43→    status: str,
    44→    resolved_findings: list[dict],
    45→    now: str,
    46→) -> None:
    47→    """Mark subjective assessments as stale when review findings are resolved.
    48→
    49→    The assessment score is preserved (not zeroed) — only a fresh review import
    50→    should change dimension scores.  The stale marker tells the UI to prompt
    51→    for a re-review.
    52→    """
    53→    assessments = state.get("subjective_assessments")
    54→    if not isinstance(assessments, dict) or not assessments:
    55→        return
    56→
    57→    touched_dimensions: set[str] = set()
    58→    for finding in resolved_findings:
    59→        if finding.get("detector") != "review":
    60→            continue
    61→        dimension = str(finding.get("detail", {}).get("dimension", "")).strip()
    62→        if dimension:
    63→            touched_dimensions.add(dimension)
    64→
    65→    for dimension in sorted(touched_dimensions):
    66→        if dimension not in assessments:
    67→            continue
    68→
    69→        payload = assessments.get(dimension)
    70→        if isinstance(payload, dict):
    71→            payload["needs_review_refresh"] = True
    72→            payload["refresh_reason"] = f"review_finding_{status}"
    73→            payload["stale_since"] = now
    74→        else:
    75→            assessments[dimension] = {
    76→                "score": coerce_assessment_score(payload) or 0.0,
    77→                "needs_review_refresh": True,
    78→                "refresh_reason": f"review_finding_{status}",
    79→                "stale_since": now,
    80→            }

    83→def match_findings(
    84→    state: StateModel, pattern: str, status_filter: str = "open"
    85→) -> list[dict]:
    86→    """Return findings matching *pattern* with the given status."""
    87→    ensure_state_defaults(state)
    88→    return [
    89→        finding
    90→        for finding_id, finding in state["findings"].items()
    91→        if not finding.get("suppressed")
    92→        if (status_filter == "all" or finding["status"] == status_filter)
    93→        and _matches_pattern(finding_id, finding, pattern)
    94→    ]

def review_finding_snapshot_hash(state: StateModel) -> str:
    """Hash open review finding IDs to detect changes.

    Returns empty string when there are no open review findings.
    """
    findings = state.get("findings", {})
    review_ids = sorted(
        fid for fid, f in findings.items()
        if f.get("status") == "open"
        and f.get("detector") in ("review", "concerns")
    )

def _print_next_command(state: dict) -> str:
    remaining = sum(
        1
        for finding in state["findings"].values()
        if finding["status"] == "open"
        and not finding.get("suppressed")
    )
    next_command = "desloppify scan"
    if remaining > 0:
        suffix = "s" if remaining != 1 else ""
        print(
            colorize(
                f"\n  {remaining} finding{suffix} remaining — run `desloppify next`",
                "dim",
            )
        )
        next_command = "desloppify next"
    print(colorize(f"  Next command: `{next_command}`", "dim"))
    print()
    return next_command
```

# Triage Reset Issue Trace

## Key Function: review_finding_snapshot_hash()
Location: desloppify/engine/_plan/stale_dimensions.py:299-312

```python
def review_finding_snapshot_hash(state: StateModel) -> str:
    """Hash open review finding IDs to detect changes.
    
    Returns empty string when there are no open review findings.
    """
    findings = state.get("findings", {})
    review_ids = sorted(
        fid for fid, f in findings.items()
        if f.get("status") == "open"
        and f.get("detector") in ("review", "concerns")
    )
    if not review_ids:
        return ""
    return hashlib.sha256("|".join(review_ids).encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
```

KEY INSIGHT: The hash is ONLY based on:
1. Findings with status == "open"
2. Detector in ("review", "concerns")

## When Triage Re-injects

Function: `sync_triage_needed()` in stale_dimensions.py:327-361

```python
def sync_triage_needed(
    plan: PlanModel,
    state: StateModel,
) -> TriageSyncResult:
    """Inject 4 triage stage IDs at front of queue when review findings change.
    
    Only injects stages not already confirmed in ``epic_triage_meta``.
    Never auto-prunes — only explicit completion removes them.
    """
    ...
    current_hash = review_finding_snapshot_hash(state)
    last_hash = meta.get("finding_snapshot_hash", "")
    
    # If hash changed and no stages present, inject unconfirmed stages
    if current_hash and current_hash != last_hash and not already_present:
        # ... inject triage stages
```

## THE BUG: Race Condition in Resolve → Scan Flow

### Step 1: User runs `plan done` to resolve items
Location: desloppify/engine/_plan/operations.py, or resolve command

When a user resolves findings (e.g., marking them as "fixed", "wontfix"), the 
findings' status changes from "open" to another status.

### Step 2: If findings are review/concerns, the hash changes
When review findings are resolved:
- OLD hash: SHA256(review_id1 | review_id2 | review_id3)
- NEW hash: SHA256(review_id1 | review_id2)  [id3 now has status != "open"]

### Step 3: User runs `scan` 
The scan reconciliation runs _reconcile_plan_post_scan():

```
_reconcile_plan_post_scan(runtime)
  ├─ load_plan()
  ├─ sync_triage_needed(plan, runtime.state)  <-- LINE 225
  │   └─ current_hash = review_finding_snapshot_hash(state)
  │   └─ last_hash = meta.get("finding_snapshot_hash", "")
  │   └─ if current_hash != last_hash and not already_present:
  │       └─ INJECT TRIAGE STAGES!
  └─ save_plan()
```

### Step 4: The Hash Never Gets Updated
When triage completes, line 264 in triage_handlers.py:

```python
current_hash = review_finding_snapshot_hash(state)
meta["finding_snapshot_hash"] = current_hash
meta["triage_stages"] = {}  # clear stages on completion
```

BUT: When the user resolves a queue item, this update NEVER happens because:
- Resolve is in resolve/cmd.py (not triage_handlers.py)
- Resolve only updates plan.json, not epic_triage_meta["finding_snapshot_hash"]
- The snapshot hash remains pointing at the OLD set of open review findings

## Example Scenario

1. Initial state: review findings [A, B, C] are open
   - finding_snapshot_hash = hash(A|B|C)
   - triage_stages = {observe: {...}, reflect: {...}, ...}
   - User completes triage

2. User works through queue and resolves findings A and B
   - Review findings now: [C]
   - But meta["finding_snapshot_hash"] is STILL hash(A|B|C)
   - Plan queue is progressing, triage stages are cleared

3. User runs `scan`
   - new_hash = review_finding_snapshot_hash(state) = hash(C)
   - old_hash = meta.get("finding_snapshot_hash") = hash(A|B|C)
   - new_hash != old_hash → TRIAGE RE-INJECTS!
   - The 4 triage stage IDs get re-added to the queue
   - This effectively "resets" the user's progress

## Root Cause
The snapshot hash is only updated when:
1. Triage completes (line 264, triage_handlers.py)
2. Triage starts (line 314, triage_handlers.py) - clears stages

It is NOT updated when:
- A resolve/fix operation removes findings from the queue
- Manual queue edits change the set of open review findings
- New review findings are added to the state

## The Fix Needed

The snapshot hash needs to be updated in one of these places:
1. When findings are resolved (resolve/cmd.py)
2. When any plan operation completes that affects queue items
3. During scan reconciliation, BEFORE checking if triage should re-inject
```

# COMPREHENSIVE TRIAGE RESET BUG ANALYSIS

## THE PROBLEM
After completing triage and resolving queue items, running `scan` causes triage to re-inject automatically, "resetting" the user's progress.

---

## PART 1: THE SNAPSHOT HASH MECHANISM

### What is `review_finding_snapshot_hash()`?
Location: `desloppify/engine/_plan/stale_dimensions.py:299-312`

```python
def review_finding_snapshot_hash(state: StateModel) -> str:
    """Hash open review finding IDs to detect changes."""
    findings = state.get("findings", {})
    review_ids = sorted(
        fid for fid, f in findings.items()
        if f.get("status") == "open"  # <-- KEY: ONLY OPEN findings
        and f.get("detector") in ("review", "concerns")
    )
    if not review_ids:
        return ""
    return hashlib.sha256("|".join(review_ids).encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
```

**KEY INSIGHT**: This hash represents the SET OF OPEN REVIEW FINDINGS.
- When a review finding is marked as "fixed", "wontfix", etc. → status changes from "open"
- Hash changes because the set of open review findings changed

---

## PART 2: WHEN TRIAGE RE-INJECTS

### Function: `sync_triage_needed()` 
Location: `desloppify/engine/_plan/stale_dimensions.py:327-361`

```python
def sync_triage_needed(plan: PlanModel, state: StateModel) -> TriageSyncResult:
    """Inject 4 triage stage IDs at front of queue when review findings change."""
    
    # ... initialization ...
    
    current_hash = review_finding_snapshot_hash(state)
    last_hash = meta.get("finding_snapshot_hash", "")
    
    # CRITICAL: If hash changed AND no stages present, inject unconfirmed stages
    if current_hash and current_hash != last_hash and not already_present:
        insert_at = _after_promoted(order, plan)
        for sid, name in zip(TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS, stage_names):
            if name not in confirmed and sid not in existing:
                order.insert(insert_at + injected_count, sid)
                injected_count += 1
        if injected_count:
            result.injected = True
    return result
```

**Condition for Re-injection**:
1. `current_hash` is not empty (has open review findings) 
2. `current_hash != last_hash` (review findings changed)
3. `not already_present` (triage stages not already in queue)

---

## PART 3: WHERE THE HASH IS UPDATED

### Location 1: When Triage COMPLETES
File: `desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage_handlers.py:264`

```python
def _cmd_triage_finish(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    # ... triage completion logic ...
    
    current_hash = review_finding_snapshot_hash(state)
    meta["finding_snapshot_hash"] = current_hash  # <-- UPDATE
    meta["triage_stages"] = {}  # clear stages
    save_plan(plan)
```

At this point:
- The hash is updated to represent the CURRENT set of open review findings
- Triage stages are cleared
- User expects to proceed with implementation

### Location 2: When Triage STARTS (via epic_triage.py)
File: `desloppify/engine/_plan/epic_triage.py:600`

```python
plan["epic_triage_meta"] = {
    "triaged_ids": open_review_ids,
    "last_run": now,
    "version": version,
    "dismissed_ids": dismissed_ids,
    "finding_snapshot_hash": current_hash,  # <-- SET at start
    "strategy_summary": triage.strategy_summary,
    "trigger": trigger,
}
```

### Location 3: Stage Persistence (intermediate snapshots)
File: `desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/stage_persistence.py:13`

```python
meta["stage_snapshot_hash"] = review_finding_snapshot_hash(state)
```

This tracks the snapshot at each stage, but different from finding_snapshot_hash.

---

## PART 4: THE BUG - WHEN THE HASH IS NOT UPDATED

### Scenario: User Resolves Review Findings

When a user marks a REVIEW FINDING as resolved (fixed, wontfix, false_positive):

1. **Resolve Command Path** (`desloppify/app/commands/resolve/cmd.py:48-159`)
   ```python
   def cmd_resolve(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
       state_file = state_path(args)
       state = state_mod.load_state(state_file)
       
       all_resolved = _resolve_all_patterns(state, args, ...)
       _save_state_or_exit(state, state_file)  # <-- State saved
       
       if has_living_plan():
           plan = load_plan()
           purged = purge_ids(plan, all_resolved)  # <-- Removes from queue
           append_log_entry(plan, "resolve", finding_ids=all_resolved, ...)
           save_plan(plan)  # <-- Plan saved
   ```
   
   **What happens**: Findings are removed from the queue, but the plan's 
   `epic_triage_meta["finding_snapshot_hash"]` is NEVER updated!

2. **Plan Skip Command Path** (`desloppify/app/commands/plan/override_handlers.py:155-236`)
   ```python
   def cmd_plan_skip(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
       # ... skip logic ...
       if kind in ("permanent", "false_positive"):
           state_data = state_mod.load_state(state_file)
           status = "wontfix" if kind == "permanent" else "false_positive"
           for fid in finding_ids:
               state_mod.resolve_findings(
                   state_data, fid, status, note or "", attestation=attestation
               )  # <-- Changes status in state
       
       count = skip_items(plan, finding_ids, kind=kind, ...)
       append_log_entry(plan, "skip", ...)
       _save_plan_state_transactional(plan=plan, state_data=state_data, ...)
   ```
   
   **What happens**: Review findings are marked as wontfix/false_positive in state,
   removed from queue, but `epic_triage_meta["finding_snapshot_hash"]` is NOT updated!

### The Critical Moment: When User Runs `scan`

File: `desloppify/app/commands/scan/scan_workflow.py:192-266`

```python
def _reconcile_plan_post_scan(runtime: "ScanRuntime") -> None:
    """Reconcile plan queue metadata and stale subjective review dimensions."""
    
    plan = load_plan(plan_path)
    
    # ... other syncs ...
    
    triage_sync = sync_triage_needed(plan, runtime.state)  # <-- LINE 225
    if triage_sync.changes:
        dirty = True
        if triage_sync.injected:
            print("  Plan: planning mode needed — review findings changed...")
            append_log_entry(plan, "sync_triage", ...)
    
    if dirty:
        save_plan(plan, plan_path)
```

**What happens**:
1. `sync_triage_needed(plan, runtime.state)` is called
2. Inside, it computes:
   ```
   current_hash = review_finding_snapshot_hash(runtime.state)
   last_hash = plan["epic_triage_meta"].get("finding_snapshot_hash", "")
   ```
3. If review findings were resolved:
   - `current_hash` = hash of REMAINING open review findings
   - `last_hash` = hash from when triage completed (includes the now-resolved findings)
   - **They don't match!** → Triage re-injects!

### Example Timeline

```
TIME 0: Initial Scan
  - Open review findings: [review_001, review_002, review_003]
  - hash_v0 = hash("review_001|review_002|review_003")

TIME 1: Triage Completes
  - epic_triage_meta["finding_snapshot_hash"] = hash_v0
  - epic_triage_meta["triage_stages"] = {} (cleared)
  - User proceeds with implementation

TIME 2: User Resolves Some Findings
  - User runs: desloppify resolve review_001 --status fixed
  - State: review_001.status = "fixed" (no longer "open")
  - Open review findings: [review_002, review_003]
  - hash_v1 = hash("review_002|review_003")
  - BUT: epic_triage_meta["finding_snapshot_hash"] still = hash_v0  <-- NOT UPDATED

TIME 3: User Runs Scan
  - Scan completes
  - _reconcile_plan_post_scan() runs
  - sync_triage_needed() computes:
    - current_hash = hash("review_002|review_003") = hash_v1
    - last_hash = hash_v0 (from epic_triage_meta)
    - hash_v1 != hash_v0 → RE-INJECT TRIAGE STAGES!
  
  ❌ RESULT: The 4 triage stages are re-added to the front of the queue!
```

---

## ROOT CAUSE SUMMARY

The snapshot hash is updated in ONLY TWO PLACES:
1. When triage completes (`triage_handlers.py:264`)
2. When triage is initially created (`epic_triage.py:600`)

It is NOT updated when:
- A finding is resolved via `resolve` command
- A finding is skipped as permanent/false_positive via `plan skip`
- A finding is manually reopened via `plan unskip`
- A finding is removed from the queue via `plan done`
- ANY operation that changes the set of open review findings

---

## THE FIX STRATEGIES

### Strategy 1: Update Hash After Any State Change (Conservative)
After any operation that might resolve findings, update the hash:
- In `resolve/cmd.py:91` (after `_save_state_or_exit`)
- In `override_handlers.py:222-230` (after state save for skip/unskip)

### Strategy 2: Update Hash During Scan Reconciliation (Aggressive)
Before calling `sync_triage_needed()`, update the hash to the current value:
- In `scan_workflow.py:225` (before sync_triage_needed)
- This catches all cases where the hash drifted

### Strategy 3: Change Detection Logic (Semantic)
Modify `sync_triage_needed()` to:
- Only re-inject if NEW findings appeared (not just open set changed)
- Or only re-inject if triage was never run before

---

## RECOMMENDED FIX
Update the snapshot hash BEFORE checking for triage re-injection during scan reconciliation.
This is the safest location because:
1. It catches ALL pathways that modify state
2. It's centralized in one place
3. It's closest to where the re-injection decision is made
4. It doesn't require changes to multiple handlers

Location: `desloppify/app/commands/scan/scan_workflow.py:225`

Before:
```python
triage_sync = sync_triage_needed(plan, runtime.state)
```

After:
```python
# Ensure snapshot hash is current before checking for triage re-injection
if has_triage_completed(plan):
    from desloppify.engine._plan.stale_dimensions import review_finding_snapshot_hash
    current_hash = review_finding_snapshot_hash(runtime.state)
    plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})["finding_snapshot_hash"] = current_hash

triage_sync = sync_triage_needed(plan, runtime.state)
```
```

## Summary

I have completed a thorough investigation of the triage reset issue. Here's what I found:

### **The Root Cause**

The triage system uses a **snapshot hash** (`review_finding_snapshot_hash()`) to detect when review findings change and needs to re-run triage. This hash is computed from the set of **open** review/concerns findings. 

**The bug occurs because:**

1. **When triage completes** (in `triage_handlers.py:264`), the hash is saved to `epic_triage_meta["finding_snapshot_hash"]` representing the findings at that moment.

2. **When the user resolves findings** (via `resolve/cmd.py` or `plan skip`), the findings' status changes from "open" to "fixed"/"wontfix"/etc., which means:
   - The set of **open** review findings shrinks
   - The hash **should** be updated in the plan
   - **But it isn't** — the hash remains unchanged in `epic_triage_meta`

3. **When the user runs `scan`** (in `scan_workflow.py:225`), the reconciliation logic runs:
   - It computes `current_hash` = the actual hash of remaining open review findings
   - It gets `last_hash` = the old hash from `epic_triage_meta` (from when triage completed)
   - Since findings were resolved, `current_hash != last_hash`
   - **Triage stages are automatically re-injected** into the queue!

### **Complete Flow Diagram**

```
Triage Completes (TIME 1)
└─ meta["finding_snapshot_hash"] = hash(review_001|review_002|review_003)
└─ meta["triage_stages"] = {} (cleared)
└─ User proceeds with implementation

User Resolves Findings (TIME 2)
└─ review_001.status = "fixed" (no longer "open")
└─ Plan queue is updated, triage_stages remain empty
└─ BUT: meta["finding_snapshot_hash"] is NEVER updated ✗

User Runs Scan (TIME 3)
└─ current_hash = hash(review_002|review_003)  [remaining open findings]
└─ last_hash = hash(review_001|review_002|review_003)  [from step TIME 1]
└─ current_hash != last_hash → TRIAGE RE-INJECTS! ✗
```

### **Where the Hash is Updated vs NOT Updated**

**ONLY updated in:**
- `triage_handlers.py:264` — when triage completes
- `epic_triage.py:600` — when triage is initially created

**NOT updated when:**
- Findings are resolved via `resolve` command (line 91)
- Findings are skipped as permanent/false_positive via `plan skip` (line 222-230)
- Findings are reopened via `plan unskip`
- Any operation changes the set of open review findings

### **Affected Code Paths**

1. `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/resolve/cmd.py:48-159`
   - Resolves findings, saves state, purges from plan
   - Does NOT update `epic_triage_meta["finding_snapshot_hash"]`

2. `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/override_handlers.py:155-236`
   - Skips findings as permanent/false_positive
   - Calls `state_mod.resolve_findings()` which changes finding status
   - Does NOT update the triage snapshot hash

3. `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/scan/scan_workflow.py:225`
   - Calls `sync_triage_needed()` which checks if hash changed
   - This is where the re-injection decision is made

4. `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/stale_dimensions.py:327-361`
   - `sync_triage_needed()` implements the re-injection logic
   - Triggered during every scan reconciliation

### **The Schema**

The plan's `epic_triage_meta` dict tracks:
- `finding_snapshot_hash`: SHA256 hash of open review finding IDs (16 chars)
- `triage_stages`: Dict of stage metadata during active triage
- `triaged_ids`: List of finding IDs that were part of the last triage
- `strategy_summary`: The triage strategy text

When triage completes, `triage_stages` is cleared but `finding_snapshot_hash` is saved.

**The mismatch occurs because:** The hash is not kept in sync when `triage_stages` is empty and the user is working through the queue.

1→"""Flat directory detection — directories with too many source files."""
     2→
     3→import logging
     4→from collections import Counter
     5→from pathlib import Path
     6→
     7→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
     8→
     9→from desloppify.core.file_paths import resolve_scan_file
    10→
    11→THIN_WRAPPER_NAMES = frozenset(
    12→    {
    13→        "components",
    14→        "hooks",
    15→        "utils",
    16→        "services",
    17→        "state",
    18→        "contexts",
    19→        "contracts",
    20→        "types",
    21→        "models",
    22→        "adapters",
    23→        "helpers",
    24→        "core",
    25→        "common",
    26→    }
    27→)
    28→
    29→
    30→def format_flat_dir_summary(entry: dict) -> str:
    31→    """Render a human-readable summary for a flat/fragmented directory entry."""
    32→    kind = str(entry.get("kind", "overload"))
    33→    file_count = int(entry.get("file_count", 0))
    34→    child_dir_count = int(entry.get("child_dir_count", 0))
    35→    combined_score = int(entry.get("combined_score", file_count))
    36→    sparse_child_count = int(entry.get("sparse_child_count", 0))
    37→    sparse_file_threshold = int(entry.get("sparse_child_file_threshold", 1))
    38→    parent_sibling_count = int(entry.get("parent_sibling_count", 0))
    39→    wrapper_item_count = int(entry.get("wrapper_item_count", 0))
    40→    if kind == "fragmented":
    41→        return (
    42→            "Directory fragmentation: "
    43→            f"{file_count} files, {child_dir_count} child dirs "
    44→            f"(combined {combined_score}); "
    45→            f"{sparse_child_count}/{child_dir_count} child dirs have <= "
    46→            f"{sparse_file_threshold} file(s) — consider flattening/grouping"
    47→        )
    48→    if kind == "overload_fragmented":
    49→        return (
    50→            "Directory overload: "
    51→            f"{file_count} files, {child_dir_count} child dirs "
    52→            f"(combined {combined_score}); "
    53→            f"{sparse_child_count}/{child_dir_count} child dirs have <= "
    54→            f"{sparse_file_threshold} file(s)"
    55→        )
    56→    if kind == "thin_wrapper":
    57→        return (
    58→            "Thin wrapper directory: "
    59→            f"{file_count} files, {child_dir_count} child dirs "
    60→            f"({wrapper_item_count} item) in parent with "
    61→            f"{parent_sibling_count} sibling dirs — consider flattening"
    62→        )
    63→    return (
    64→        "Directory overload: "
    65→        f"{file_count} files, {child_dir_count} child dirs "
    66→        f"(combined {combined_score}) — consider grouping by domain"
    67→    )
    68→
    69→
    70→def detect_flat_dirs(
    71→    path: Path,
    72→    file_finder,
    73→    threshold: int = 20,
    74→    *,
    75→    child_dir_threshold: int = 10,
    76→    child_dir_weight: int = 3,
    77→    combined_threshold: int = 30,
    78→    sparse_parent_child_threshold: int = 8,
    79→    sparse_child_file_threshold: int = 1,
    80→    sparse_child_count_threshold: int = 6,
    81→    sparse_child_ratio_threshold: float = 0.7,
    82→    thin_wrapper_parent_sibling_threshold: int = 10,
    83→    thin_wrapper_max_file_count: int = 1,
    84→    thin_wrapper_max_child_dir_count: int = 1,
    85→    thin_wrapper_names: tuple[str, ...] = (
    86→        "components",
    87→        "hooks",
    88→        "utils",
    89→        "services",
    90→        "state",
    91→        "contexts",
    92→        "contracts",
    93→        "types",
    94→        "models",
    95→        "adapters",
    96→        "helpers",
    97→        "core",
    98→        "common",
    99→    ),
   100→) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
   101→    """Find overloaded/fragmented directories using count and fan-out heuristics."""
   102→    files = file_finder(path)
   103→    scan_root = path.resolve()
   104→    dir_counts: Counter[str] = Counter()
   105→    child_dirs: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
   106→    for f in files:
   107→        try:
   108→            resolved_file = resolve_scan_file(f, scan_root=path).resolve()
   109→            parent_path = resolved_file.parent
   110→            parent_rel = parent_path.relative_to(scan_root)
   111→        except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
   112→            logger.debug("Skipping unresolvable file %s: %s", f, exc)
   113→            continue
   114→
   115→        parent = str((scan_root / parent_rel).resolve())
   116→        dir_counts[parent] += 1
   117→        # Track direct subdirectory fan-out for every ancestor.
   118→        parts = parent_rel.parts
   119→        for idx in range(len(parts) - 1):
   120→            ancestor = (scan_root / Path(*parts[: idx + 1])).resolve()
   121→            child = (scan_root / Path(*parts[: idx + 2])).resolve()
   122→            ancestor_key = str(ancestor)
   123→            child_dirs.setdefault(ancestor_key, set()).add(str(child))
   124→
   125→    all_dirs: set[str] = set(dir_counts.keys())
   126→    all_dirs.update(child_dirs.keys())
   127→    for children in child_dirs.values():
   128→        all_dirs.update(children)
   129→
   130→    thin_names = {name.lower() for name in thin_wrapper_names}
   131→    if not thin_names:
   132→        thin_names = set(THIN_WRAPPER_NAMES)
   133→
   134→    entries = []
   135→    for dir_path in sorted(all_dirs):
   136→        file_count = int(dir_counts.get(dir_path, 0))
   137→        direct_children = child_dirs.get(dir_path, set())
   138→        direct_child_count = len(direct_children)
   139→        combined_score = file_count + (child_dir_weight * direct_child_count)
   140→        has_local_files = dir_path in dir_counts
   141→
   142→        if has_local_files:
   143→            overloaded = (
   144→                file_count >= threshold
   145→                or direct_child_count >= child_dir_threshold
   146→                or combined_score >= combined_threshold
   147→            )
   148→            if overloaded:
   149→                entries.append(
   150→                    {
   151→                        "directory": dir_path,
   152→                        "file_count": file_count,
   153→                        "child_dir_count": direct_child_count,
   154→                        "combined_score": combined_score,
   155→                        "kind": "overload",
   156→                    }
   157→                )
   158→                continue
   159→            # Conservative anti-fragmentation signal:
   160→            # only flag when a parent has many child dirs and most are single-file leaves.
   161→            sparse_child_count = 0
   162→            for child in direct_children:
   163→                child_file_count = int(dir_counts.get(child, 0))
   164→                child_child_count = len(child_dirs.get(child, set()))
   165→                if (
   166→                    child_file_count <= sparse_child_file_threshold
   167→                    and child_child_count == 0
   168→                ):
   169→                    sparse_child_count += 1
   170→            sparse_child_ratio = (
   171→                float(sparse_child_count) / float(direct_child_count)
   172→                if direct_child_count
   173→                else 0.0
   174→            )
   175→            fragmented = (
   176→                direct_child_count >= sparse_parent_child_threshold
   177→                and sparse_child_count >= sparse_child_count_threshold
   178→                and sparse_child_ratio >= sparse_child_ratio_threshold
   179→            )
   180→            if fragmented:
   181→                entries.append(
   182→                    {
   183→                        "directory": dir_path,
   184→                        "file_count": file_count,
   185→                        "child_dir_count": direct_child_count,
   186→                        "combined_score": combined_score,
   187→                        "kind": "fragmented",
   188→                        "sparse_child_count": sparse_child_count,
   189→                        "sparse_child_ratio": sparse_child_ratio,
   190→                        "sparse_child_file_threshold": sparse_child_file_threshold,
   191→                    }
   192→                )
   193→                continue
   194→
   195→        dir_name = Path(dir_path).name.lower()
   196→        parent_key = str(Path(dir_path).parent)
   197→        parent_sibling_count = len(child_dirs.get(parent_key, set()))
   198→        wrapper_item_count = file_count + direct_child_count
   199→        thin_wrapper = (
   200→            dir_name in thin_names
   201→            and wrapper_item_count == 1
   202→            and file_count <= thin_wrapper_max_file_count
   203→            and direct_child_count <= thin_wrapper_max_child_dir_count
   204→            and parent_sibling_count >= thin_wrapper_parent_sibling_threshold
   205→        )
   206→        if thin_wrapper:
   207→            entries.append(
   208→                {
   209→                    "directory": dir_path,
   210→                    "file_count": file_count,
   211→                    "child_dir_count": direct_child_count,
   212→                    "combined_score": combined_score,
   213→                    "kind": "thin_wrapper",
   214→                    "parent_sibling_count": parent_sibling_count,
   215→                    "wrapper_item_count": wrapper_item_count,
   216→                }
   217→            )
   218→    return sorted(
   219→        entries,
   220→        key=lambda e: (
   221→            -int(e["combined_score"]),
   222→            -int(e.get("parent_sibling_count", 0)),
   223→            -int(e.get("sparse_child_count", 0)),
   224→            -int(e["child_dir_count"]),
   225→            -int(e["file_count"]),
   226→        ),
   227→    ), len(all_dirs)
   228→
