   120→def _validate_dimension_note(
   121→    key: str,
   122→    note_raw: object,
   123→) -> tuple[list[object], str, str, str, str]:
   124→    """Validate a single dimension_notes entry and return parsed fields.
   125→
   126→    Returns (evidence, impact_scope, fix_scope, confidence, issues_preventing_higher_score).
   127→    Raises ValueError on invalid structure.
   128→    """
   129→    if not isinstance(note_raw, dict):
   130→        raise ValueError(
   131→            f"dimension_notes missing object for assessed dimension: {key}"
   132→        )
   133→    evidence = note_raw.get("evidence")
   134→    impact_scope = note_raw.get("impact_scope")
   135→    fix_scope = note_raw.get("fix_scope")
   136→    if not isinstance(evidence, list) or not evidence:
   137→        raise ValueError(
   138→            f"dimension_notes.{key}.evidence must be a non-empty array"
   139→        )
   140→    if not isinstance(impact_scope, str) or not impact_scope.strip():
   141→        raise ValueError(
   142→            f"dimension_notes.{key}.impact_scope must be a non-empty string"
   143→        )
   144→    if not isinstance(fix_scope, str) or not fix_scope.strip():
   145→        raise ValueError(
   146→            f"dimension_notes.{key}.fix_scope must be a non-empty string"
   147→        )
   148→
   149→    confidence_raw = str(note_raw.get("confidence", "medium")).strip().lower()
   150→    confidence = (
   151→        confidence_raw if confidence_raw in {"high", "medium", "low"} else "medium"
   152→    )
   153→    issues_note = str(note_raw.get(DIMENSION_NOTE_ISSUES_KEY, "")).strip()
   154→    if not issues_note:
   155→        issues_note = str(note_raw.get(LEGACY_DIMENSION_NOTE_ISSUES_KEY, "")).strip()
   156→    return evidence, impact_scope, fix_scope, confidence, issues_note
   157→
   158→
   159→def _normalize_abstraction_sub_axes(
   160→    note_raw: dict[str, object],
   161→    abstraction_sub_axes: tuple[str, ...],
   162→) -> dict[str, float]:
   163→    """Extract and clamp abstraction_fitness sub-axis scores from a note."""
   164→    sub_axes_raw = note_raw.get("sub_axes")
   165→    if sub_axes_raw is not None and not isinstance(sub_axes_raw, dict):
   166→        raise ValueError(
   167→            "dimension_notes.abstraction_fitness.sub_axes must be an object"
   168→        )
   169→    if not isinstance(sub_axes_raw, dict):
   170→        return {}
   171→
   172→    normalized: dict[str, float] = {}
   173→    for axis in abstraction_sub_axes:
   174→        axis_value = sub_axes_raw.get(axis)
   175→        if axis_value is None:
   176→            continue
   177→        if isinstance(axis_value, bool) or not isinstance(
   178→            axis_value, int | float
   179→        ):
   180→            raise ValueError(
   181→                f"dimension_notes.abstraction_fitness.sub_axes.{axis} "
   182→                "must be numeric"
   183→            )
   184→        normalized[axis] = round(
   185→            max(0.0, min(100.0, float(axis_value))),
   186→            1,
   187→        )
   188→    return normalized
   189→
   190→
   191→def _normalize_findings(
   192→    raw_findings: object,
   193→    dimension_notes: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
   194→    *,
   195→    max_batch_findings: int,
   196→    allowed_dims: set[str],
   197→    low_score_dimensions: set[str] | None = None,
   198→) -> list[NormalizedBatchFinding]:
   199→    """Validate and normalize the findings array from a batch payload."""
   200→    if not isinstance(raw_findings, list):
   201→        raise ValueError("findings must be an array")
   202→
   203→    findings: list[NormalizedBatchFinding] = []
   204→    errors: list[str] = []
   205→    for idx, item in enumerate(raw_findings):
   206→        finding: ReviewFindingPayload | None
   207→        finding, finding_errors = validate_review_finding_payload(
   208→            item,
   209→            label=f"findings[{idx}]",
   210→            allowed_dimensions=allowed_dims,
   211→            allow_dismissed=False,
   212→        )
   213→        if finding_errors:
   214→            errors.extend(finding_errors)
   215→            continue
   216→        assert finding is not None
   217→
   218→        dim = finding["dimension"]
   219→        note = dimension_notes.get(dim, {})
   220→        impact_scope = str(
   221→            (item if isinstance(item, dict) else {}).get(
   222→                "impact_scope", note.get("impact_scope", "")
   223→            )
   224→        ).strip()
   225→        fix_scope = str(
   226→            (item if isinstance(item, dict) else {}).get(
   227→                "fix_scope", note.get("fix_scope", "")
   228→            )
   229→        ).strip()
   230→        if not impact_scope or not fix_scope:
   231→            errors.append(
   232→                f"findings[{idx}] requires impact_scope and fix_scope "
   233→                "(or dimension_notes defaults)"
   234→            )
   235→            continue
   236→        findings.append(
   237→            NormalizedBatchFinding(
   238→                dimension=finding["dimension"],
   239→                identifier=finding["identifier"],
   240→                summary=finding["summary"],
   241→                confidence=finding["confidence"],
   242→                suggestion=finding["suggestion"],
   243→                related_files=list(finding.get("related_files", [])),
   244→                evidence=list(finding.get("evidence", [])),
   245→                impact_scope=impact_scope,
   246→                fix_scope=fix_scope,
   247→                reasoning=str(finding.get("reasoning", "")),
   248→                evidence_lines=list(finding.get("evidence_lines", []))
   249→                if isinstance(finding.get("evidence_lines"), list)
   250→                else None,
   251→            )
   252→        )
   253→    if errors:
   254→        visible = errors[:10]
   255→        remaining = len(errors) - len(visible)
   256→        if remaining > 0:
   257→            visible.append(f"... {remaining} additional finding schema error(s) omitted")
   258→        raise ValueError("; ".join(visible))
   259→    if len(findings) <= max_batch_findings:
   260→        return findings
   261→
   262→    required_dims = set(low_score_dimensions or set())
   263→    if not required_dims:
   264→        return findings[:max_batch_findings]
   265→
   266→    # Preserve at least one finding per low-score dimension before trimming.
   267→    selected: list[NormalizedBatchFinding] = []
   268→    selected_indexes: set[int] = set()
   269→    covered: set[str] = set()
   270→    for idx, finding in enumerate(findings):
   271→        if len(selected) >= max_batch_findings:
   272→            break
   273→        dim = finding.dimension.strip()
   274→        if dim not in required_dims or dim in covered:
   275→            continue
   276→        selected.append(finding)
   277→        selected_indexes.add(idx)
   278→        covered.add(dim)
   279→
   280→    for idx, finding in enumerate(findings):
   281→        if len(selected) >= max_batch_findings:
   282→            break
   283→        if idx in selected_indexes:
   284→            continue
   285→        selected.append(finding)
   286→    return selected
   287→
   288→
   289→def _low_score_dimensions(assessments: dict[str, float]) -> set[str]:
   290→    """Return assessed dimensions requiring explicit defect findings."""
   291→    return {
   292→        dim
   293→        for dim, score in assessments.items()
   294→        if score < LOW_SCORE_FINDING_THRESHOLD
   295→    }
   296→
   297→
   298→def _enforce_low_score_findings(
   299→    *,
   300→    assessments: dict[str, float],
   301→    findings: list[NormalizedBatchFinding],
   302→) -> None:
   303→    """Fail closed when low scores do not report explicit findings."""
   304→    required_dims = _low_score_dimensions(assessments)
   305→    if not required_dims:
   306→        return
   307→    finding_dims = {
   308→        finding.dimension.strip() for finding in findings
   309→    }
   310→    missing = sorted(dim for dim in required_dims if dim not in finding_dims)
   311→    if not missing:
   312→        return
   313→    joined = ", ".join(missing)
   314→    raise ValueError(
   315→        "low-score dimensions must include at least one explicit finding: "
   316→        f"{joined} (threshold {LOW_SCORE_FINDING_THRESHOLD:.1f})"
   317→    )
   318→
   319→
   320→def _compute_batch_quality(
   321→    assessments: dict[str, float],
   322→    findings: list[NormalizedBatchFinding],
   323→    dimension_notes: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
   324→    allowed_dims: set[str],
   325→    high_score_missing_issue_note: float,
   326→) -> dict[str, float]:
   327→    """Compute quality metrics for a single batch result."""
   328→    return {
   329→        "dimension_coverage": round(
   330→            len(assessments) / max(len(allowed_dims), 1),
   331→            3,
   332→        ),
   333→        "evidence_density": round(
   334→            sum(len(note.get("evidence", [])) for note in dimension_notes.values())
   335→            / max(len(findings), 1),
   336→            3,
   337→        ),
   338→        [REDACTED],
   339→    }
   340→
   341→
   342→def normalize_batch_result(
   343→    payload: dict[str, object],
   344→    allowed_dims: set[str],
   345→    *,
   346→    max_batch_findings: int,
   347→    abstraction_sub_axes: tuple[str, ...],
   348→) -> tuple[
   349→    dict[str, float],
   350→    list[dict[str, Any]],
   351→    dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
   352→    dict[str, float],
   353→]:
   354→    """Validate and normalize one batch payload."""
   355→    if "assessments" not in payload:
   356→        raise ValueError("payload missing required key: assessments")
   357→    if "findings" not in payload:
   358→        raise ValueError("payload missing required key: findings")
   359→
   360→    raw_assessments = payload.get("assessments")
   361→    if not isinstance(raw_assessments, dict):
   362→        raise ValueError("assessments must be an object")
   363→
   364→    raw_dimension_notes = payload.get("dimension_notes", {})
   365→    if not isinstance(raw_dimension_notes, dict):
   366→        raise ValueError("dimension_notes must be an object")
   367→
   368→    assessments: dict[str, float] = {}
   369→    dimension_notes: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
   370→    high_score_missing_issue_note = 0.0
   371→    for key, value in raw_assessments.items():
   372→        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
   373→            continue
   374→        if key not in allowed_dims:
   375→            continue
   376→        if isinstance(value, bool):
   377→            continue
   378→        if not isinstance(value, int | float):
   379→            continue
   380→        score = round(max(0.0, min(100.0, float(value))), 1)
   381→
   382→        note_raw = raw_dimension_notes.get(key)
   383→        evidence, impact_scope, fix_scope, confidence, issues_note = (
   384→            _validate_dimension_note(key, note_raw)
   385→        )
   386→        assert isinstance(note_raw, dict)
   387→        if score > HIGH_SCORE_ISSUES_NOTE_THRESHOLD and not issues_note:
   388→            high_score_missing_issue_note += 1
   389→
   390→        normalized_sub_axes: dict[str, float] = {}
   391→        if key == "abstraction_fitness" and isinstance(note_raw, dict):
   392→            normalized_sub_axes = _normalize_abstraction_sub_axes(
   393→                note_raw, abstraction_sub_axes
   394→            )
   395→
   396→        assessments[key] = score
   397→        dimension_notes[key] = {
   398→            "evidence": [str(item).strip() for item in evidence if str(item).strip()],
   399→            "impact_scope": impact_scope.strip(),
   400→            "fix_scope": fix_scope.strip(),
   401→            "confidence": confidence,
   402→            DIMENSION_NOTE_ISSUES_KEY: issues_note,
   403→        }
   404→        if normalized_sub_axes:
   405→            dimension_notes[key]["sub_axes"] = normalized_sub_axes
   406→
   407→    findings = _normalize_findings(
   408→        payload.get("findings"),
   409→        dimension_notes,
   410→        max_batch_findings=max_batch_findings,
   411→        allowed_dims=allowed_dims,
   412→        low_score_dimensions=_low_score_dimensions(assessments),
   413→    )
   414→    _enforce_low_score_findings(assessments=assessments, findings=findings)
   415→
   416→    quality = _compute_batch_quality(
   417→        assessments,
   418→        findings,
   419→        dimension_notes,
   420→        allowed_dims,
   421→        high_score_missing_issue_note,
   422→    )
   423→    return (
   424→        assessments,
   425→        [finding.to_payload() for finding in findings],
   426→        dimension_notes,
   427→        quality,
   428→    )
   429→
   430→
   431→def assessment_weight(
   432→    *,
   433→    dimension: str,
   434→    findings: list[dict[str, Any]],
   435→    dimension_notes: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
   436→) -> float:
   437→    """Evidence-weighted assessment score weight with a neutral floor.
   438→
   439→    Weighting is evidence-based and score-independent: the raw score does not
   440→    influence how much weight a batch contributes during merge.
   441→    """
   442→    note = dimension_notes.get(dimension, {})
   443→    note_evidence = len(note.get("evidence", [])) if isinstance(note, dict) else 0
   444→    finding_count = sum(
   445→        1
   446→        for finding in findings
   447→        if str(finding.get("dimension", "")).strip() == dimension
   448→    )
   449→    return float(1 + note_evidence + finding_count)
   450→
   451→
   452→def _finding_pressure_by_dimension(
   453→    findings: list[dict[str, Any]],
   454→    *,
   455→    dimension_notes: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
   456→) -> tuple[dict[str, float], dict[str, int]]:
   457→    """Summarize how strongly findings should pull dimension scores down."""
   458→    return _DIMENSION_SCORER.finding_pressure_by_dimension(
   459→        findings,
   460→        dimension_notes=dimension_notes,
   461→    )
   462→
   463→
   464→def _accumulate_batch_scores(
   465→    result: dict[str, Any],
   466→    *,
   467→    score_buckets: dict[str, list[tuple[float, float]]],
   468→    score_raw_by_dim: dict[str, list[float]],
   469→    merged_dimension_notes: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
   470→    abstraction_axis_scores: dict[str, list[tuple[float, float]]],
   471→    abstraction_sub_axes: tuple[str, ...],
   472→) -> None:
   473→    """Accumulate assessment scores, dimension notes, and sub-axis data from one batch."""
   474→    result_findings = result.get("findings", [])
   475→    result_notes = result.get("dimension_notes", {})
   476→    for key, score in result.get("assessments", {}).items():
   477→        if isinstance(score, bool):
   478→            continue
   479→        score_value = float(score)
   480→        weight = assessment_weight(
   481→            dimension=key,
   482→            findings=result_findings,
   483→            dimension_notes=result_notes,
   484→        )
   485→        score_buckets.setdefault(key, []).append((score_value, weight))
   486→        score_raw_by_dim.setdefault(key, []).append(score_value)
   487→
   488→        note = result_notes.get(key)
   489→        existing = merged_dimension_notes.get(key)
   490→        existing_evidence = (
   491→            len(existing.get("evidence", [])) if isinstance(existing, dict) else -1
   492→        )
   493→        current_evidence = (
   494→            len(note.get("evidence", [])) if isinstance(note, dict) else -1
   495→        )
   496→        if current_evidence > existing_evidence:
   497→            merged_dimension_notes[key] = note
   498→
   499→        if key == "abstraction_fitness" and isinstance(note, dict):
   500→            sub_axes = note.get("sub_axes")
   501→            if isinstance(sub_axes, dict):
   502→                for axis in abstraction_sub_axes:
   503→                    axis_score = sub_axes.get(axis)
   504→                    if isinstance(axis_score, bool) or not isinstance(
   505→                        axis_score, int | float
   506→                    ):
   507→                        continue
   508→                    abstraction_axis_scores[axis].append(
   509→                        (float(axis_score), weight)
   510→                    )
   511→
   512→
   513→def _finding_identity_key(finding: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
   514→    """Build a stable concept key; prefer dimension+identifier when available."""
   515→    dim = str(finding.get("dimension", "")).strip()
   516→    ident = str(finding.get("identifier", "")).strip()
   517→    if ident:
   518→        return f"{dim}::{ident}"
   519→    summary = str(finding.get("summary", "")).strip()
   520→    summary_terms = sorted(normalize_word_set(summary))
   521→    if summary_terms:
   522→        return f"{dim}::summary::{','.join(summary_terms[:8])}"
   523→    return f"{dim}::{summary}"
   524→
   525→
   526→def _merge_finding_payload(existing: dict[str, Any], incoming: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   527→    """Merge two concept-equivalent findings into the existing payload."""
   528→    merge_list_fields(existing, incoming, ("related_files", "evidence"))
   529→    # Prefer richer summary/suggestion text when they differ.
   530→    pick_longer_text(existing, incoming, "summary")
   531→    pick_longer_text(existing, incoming, "suggestion")
   532→    track_merged_from(existing, str(incoming.get("identifier", "")).strip())
   533→
   534→
   535→def _should_merge_findings(existing: dict[str, Any], incoming: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
   536→    """Check whether two key-matched findings are similar enough to merge."""
   537→    existing_summary = normalize_word_set(str(existing.get("summary", "")))
   538→    incoming_summary = normalize_word_set(str(incoming.get("summary", "")))
   539→    if existing_summary and incoming_summary:
   540→        overlap = len(existing_summary & incoming_summary)
   541→        union = len(existing_summary | incoming_summary)
   542→        if union and overlap / union >= 0.3:
   543→            return True
   544→    # Fall back to related-file overlap
   545→    existing_files = set(existing.get("related_files", []))
   546→    incoming_files = set(incoming.get("related_files", []))
   547→    if existing_files and incoming_files:
   548→        return bool(existing_files & incoming_files)
   549→    # When no corroborating signal is available, allow merge
   550→    return not existing_summary or not incoming_summary
   551→
   552→
   553→def _accumulate_batch_findings(
   554→    result: dict[str, Any],
   555→    finding_map: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
   556→) -> None:
   557→    """Deduplicate and accumulate findings from one batch into finding_map."""
   558→    suffix_counter: dict[str, int] = {}
   559→    for finding in result.get("findings", []):
   560→        [REDACTED](finding)
   561→        existing = finding_map.get(dedupe_key)
   562→        if existing is None:
   563→            finding_map[dedupe_key] = finding
   564→            continue
   565→        if _should_merge_findings(existing, finding):
   566→            _merge_finding_payload(existing, finding)
   567→        else:
   568→            # Distinct finding with reused identifier — assign unique key
   569→            count = suffix_counter.get(dedupe_key, 0) + 1
   570→            suffix_counter[dedupe_key] = count
   571→            finding_map[f"{dedupe_key}##dup{count}"] = finding
   572→
   573→
   574→def _accumulate_batch_quality(
   575→    result: dict[str, Any],
   576→    *,
   577→    coverage_values: list[float],
   578→    evidence_density_values: list[float],
   579→) -> float:
   580→    """Accumulate quality metrics from one batch. Returns high-score-missing-issues delta."""
   581→    quality = result.get("quality", {})
   582→    if not isinstance(quality, dict):
   583→        return 0.0
   584→    coverage = quality.get("dimension_coverage")
   585→    density = quality.get("evidence_density")
   586→    missing_issue_note = quality.get(REVIEW_QUALITY_HIGH_SCORE_MISSING_ISSUES_KEY)
   587→    if not isinstance(missing_issue_note, int | float):
   588→        missing_issue_note = quality.get(
   589→            LEGACY_REVIEW_QUALITY_HIGH_SCORE_MISSING_ISSUES_KEY
   590→        )
   591→    if isinstance(coverage, int | float):
   592→        coverage_values.append(float(coverage))
   593→    if isinstance(density, int | float):
   594→        evidence_density_values.append(float(density))
   595→    return (
   596→        float(missing_issue_note)
   597→        if isinstance(missing_issue_note, int | float)
   598→        else 0.0
   599→    )

   601→
   602→def _compute_merged_assessments(
   603→    score_buckets: dict[str, list[tuple[float, float]]],
   604→    score_raw_by_dim: dict[str, list[float]],
   605→    finding_pressure_by_dim: dict[str, float],
   606→    finding_count_by_dim: dict[str, int],
   607→) -> dict[str, float]:
   608→    """Compute pressure-adjusted weighted mean for each dimension."""
   609→    return _DIMENSION_SCORER.merge_scores(
   610→        score_buckets,
   611→        score_raw_by_dim,
   612→        finding_pressure_by_dim,
   613→        finding_count_by_dim,
   614→    )
   615→
   616→
   617→def _compute_abstraction_components(
   618→    merged_assessments: dict[str, float],
   619→    abstraction_axis_scores: dict[str, list[tuple[float, float]]],
   620→    *,
   621→    abstraction_sub_axes: tuple[str, ...],
   622→    abstraction_component_names: dict[str, str],
   623→) -> dict[str, float] | None:
   624→    """Compute weighted abstraction sub-axis component scores.
   625→
   626→    Returns component_scores dict, or None if abstraction_fitness is not assessed.
   627→    """
   628→    abstraction_score = merged_assessments.get("abstraction_fitness")
   629→    if abstraction_score is None:
   630→        return None
   631→
   632→    component_scores: dict[str, float] = {}
   633→    for axis in abstraction_sub_axes:
   634→        weighted = abstraction_axis_scores.get(axis, [])
   635→        if not weighted:
   636→            continue
   637→        numerator = sum(score * weight for score, weight in weighted)
   638→        denominator = sum(weight for _, weight in weighted)
   639→        if denominator <= 0:
   640→            continue
   641→        component_scores[abstraction_component_names[axis]] = round(
   642→            max(0.0, min(100.0, numerator / denominator)),
   643→            1,
   644→        )
   645→    return component_scores if component_scores else None
   646→

   653→) -> dict[str, object]:
   654→    """Deterministically merge assessments/findings across batch outputs."""
   655→    from .batch_merge import merge_batch_results as _merge_batch_results
   656→
   657→    return _merge_batch_results(
   658→        batch_results,
   659→        abstraction_sub_axes=abstraction_sub_axes,
   660→        abstraction_component_names=abstraction_component_names,
   661→    )

   272→    try:

   285→    except import_helpers_mod.ImportPayloadLoadError as exc:
   286→        import_helpers_mod.print_import_load_errors(
   287→            exc.errors,
   288→            import_file=str(import_file),
   289→            colorize_fn=colorize,

   291→        sys.exit(1)
   292→    assessment_policy: AssessmentImportPolicyModel = (

   307→    # Transactional import: only persist if all post-import guards pass.

   273→def _parse_and_validate_import(

   286→    """Parse and validate a review import file (pure function).

   308→        findings_data

   310→    if shape_errors:

   312→    assert normalized_findings_data is not None
   313→

   317→        assessment_override=assessment_override,

   323→        ]

   327→            "attested score imports require fully valid findings payloads"
   328→        ]
   329→    if override_enabled and allow_partial:

   354→                return None, ["--manual-override requires --attest"]
   355→            return findings_data, []
   356→        return None, [

   366→            return findings_data, []

   379→        visible_errors = schema_errors[:10]
   380→        remaining = len(schema_errors) - len(visible_errors)
   381→        errors = [
   382→            "findings schema validation failed for holistic import. "
   383→            "Fix payload or rerun with --allow-partial to continue."
   384→        ]
   385→        errors.extend(visible_errors)
   386→        if remaining > 0:
   387→            errors.append(f"... {remaining} additional schema error(s) omitted")
   388→        return None, errors
   389→
   390→    return findings_data, []

   670→def _execute_parallel(
   671→    *, tasks, indexes, progress_fn, error_log_fn,
   672→    max_parallel_workers, heartbeat_seconds, clock_fn,
   673→) -> list[int]:
   674→    """Run tasks in a thread pool with optional heartbeat monitoring.
   675→
   676→    Two closures (_run_one, _on_complete) share mutable executor state
   677→    (started_at, failures) under a lock — the natural pattern for thread-pool
   678→    work.
   679→    """
   680→    requested = (
   681→        int(max_parallel_workers)
   682→        if isinstance(max_parallel_workers, int) and max_parallel_workers > 0
   683→        else 8
   684→    )
   685→    max_workers = max(1, min(len(indexes), requested))

   696→
   697→    def _run_one(idx: int) -> int:
   698→        with lock:
   699→            started_at[idx] = float(clock_fn())
   700→        progress_error = _emit_progress(

   702→            details={"max_workers": max_workers},
   703→        )

   706→                idx=idx,
   707→                err=progress_error,
   708→                progress_failures=progress_failures,
   709→                lock=lock,
   710→                error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   711→            )
   712→        return tasks[idx]()
   713→
   714→    def _on_complete(future) -> None:
   715→        idx = futures[future]
   716→        with lock:
   717→            t0 = started_at.get(idx, float(clock_fn()))
   718→        elapsed = int(max(0.0, clock_fn() - t0))

   724→                failures=failures,
   725→                idx=idx,
   726→                exc=exc,
   727→            )

   118→def show_dimension_deltas(
   119→    prev: dict,
   120→    current: dict,
   121→    *,
   122→    scoring_mod,
   123→    colorize_fn,
   124→) -> None:
   125→    """Show which dimensions changed between scans (health and strict)."""

   128→        p = prev.get(dim.name, {})

   131→            continue

   133→        new_score = n.get("score", 100)
   134→        old_strict = p.get("strict", old_score)
   135→        new_strict = n.get("strict", new_score)
   136→        delta = new_score - old_score
   137→        strict_delta = new_strict - old_strict
   138→        if abs(delta) >= 0.1 or abs(strict_delta) >= 0.1:
   139→            moved.append(
   140→                (
   141→                    dim.name,
   142→                    old_score,
   143→                    new_score,
   144→                    delta,
   145→                    old_strict,
   146→                    new_strict,
   147→                    strict_delta,
   148→                )
   149→            )
   150→
   151→    if not moved:
   152→        return
   153→
   154→    print(colorize_fn("  Moved:", "dim"))
   155→    for name, old, new, delta, old_s, new_s, s_delta in sorted(
   156→        moved, key=lambda item: item[3]
   157→    ):
   158→        sign = "+" if delta > 0 else ""
   159→        color = "green" if delta > 0 else "red"

    84→def strip_c_style_comments(text: str) -> str:
    85→    """Strip // and /* */ comments while preserving string literals."""
    86→    result: list[str] = []
    87→    i = 0
    88→    in_str = None
    89→    while i < len(text):
    90→        ch = text[i]
    91→        if in_str:
    92→            if ch == "\\" and i + 1 < len(text):
    93→                result.append(text[i : i + 2])
    94→                i += 2
    95→                continue
    96→            if ch == in_str:
    97→                in_str = None
    98→            result.append(ch)
    99→            i += 1
   100→        elif ch in ('"', "'", "`"):
   101→            in_str = ch
   102→            result.append(ch)
   103→            i += 1
   104→        elif ch == "/" and i + 1 < len(text):
   105→            if text[i + 1] == "/":
   106→                nl = text.find("\n", i)
   107→                if nl == -1:
   108→                    break
   109→                i = nl
   110→            elif text[i + 1] == "*":
   111→                end = text.find("*/", i + 2)
   112→                if end == -1:
   113→                    break
   114→                i = end + 2
   115→            else:
   116→                result.append(ch)
   117→                i += 1
   118→        else:
   119→            result.append(ch)
   120→            i += 1
   121→    return "".join(result)
   122→

   124→def is_numeric(value: object) -> bool:
   125→    """Return True if *value* is an int or float but NOT a bool.
   126→
   127→    Python's ``bool`` is a subclass of ``int``, so ``isinstance(True, int)``
   128→    is ``True``.  Many JSON-derived payloads need to distinguish real numbers
   129→    from booleans; this helper centralises that guard.
   130→    """
   131→    return isinstance(value, int | float) and not isinstance(value, bool)

## Assessment: High Cyclomatic Complexity Findings

### 1. `next_parts/render.py` — 5 functions

**`_render_finding_detail` (line 88, ~43 LOC)**
SKIP. Renders a structured multi-field card; each `if` guard is a distinct optional field (`lines`, `category`, `importers`, `suggestion`, `code snippet`). Sequential rendering of heterogeneous optional fields — refactoring into sub-helpers would fragment cohesion without reducing complexity.

**`_render_score_impact` (line 133, ~57 LOC)**
FIX. The function has two separate logic branches (`detector != "review"` vs `detector == "review"`) that do similar things (compute impact, print it) but with different APIs. The `review` branch (lines 171–188) is a self-contained lookup that can be extracted as `_render_review_dimension_drag(item, dim_scores)`. The `potentials` branch can similarly be split into `_render_mechanical_impact(...)`. This reduces the function from ~57 to ~20 LOC with no loss of clarity.

**`_render_item` (line 191, ~76 LOC)**
SKIP. This is a dispatch function — it routes items to different renderers by `kind`, then handles the `explain` path for the general case. The branching on `kind` is a clean dispatch table (early returns for cluster/workflow/subjective), and the `explain` block at the end is the only place that assembles rank explanation text. Extracting `_render_explain_block(item, ...)` would be a marginal improvement but the function reads clearly as-is.

**`render_terminal_items` (line 269, ~46 LOC)**
SKIP. Queue output rendering loop with focus-cluster detection, position labeling, and compact/full card switching. The branches are mutually exclusive rendering modes — the complexity is structural to the feature.

**`render_followup_nudges` (line 378, ~146 LOC)**
FIX. This function has three distinct concerns crammed together: (1) frozen score / queue progress block rendering (lines 404–448), (2) subjective bottleneck banner (lines 457–483), and (3) subjective summary line assembly (lines 497–522). Extract `_render_score_progress_block(queue_total, plan_start_strict, breakdown, strict_score, target_strict_score)` and `_render_subjective_summary(findings_scoped, followup, subjective_entries, unassessed_subjective)`. This reduces the function to a top-level coordinator of ~20 LOC.

---

### 2. `plan/_resolve.py` — `resolve_ids_from_patterns` (line 9, ~43 LOC)

SKIP. Three-way resolution logic (state match → plan literal ID → cluster expansion) with a deduplication accumulator. Each branch handles a distinct resolution strategy; the function is already well-structured and clear. This is inherent complexity for a pattern-resolution utility.

---

### 3. `plan/override_handlers.py` — 2 functions

**`cmd_plan_skip` (line 144, ~91 LOC)**
SKIP. CLI command handler — validates skip kind, handles permanent/false_positive attestation requirements, performs state mutation, and outputs result. The three `kind` branches drive qualitatively different behavior (state-layer write, plan-layer write, or both). The complexity is inherent to the command's policy enforcement.

**`cmd_plan_done` (line 435, ~101 LOC)**
FIX. The function does four separable things: (1) `--confirm` auto-attestation, (2) synthetic ID handling with triage dependency validation, (3) cluster guard + plan log entry, and (4) delegating to `cmd_resolve`. Steps 2 and 3 can each be extracted: `_handle_synthetic_ids(args, patterns, note)` and `_log_done_action(patterns, plan, note)`. This reduces the main function to a well-labeled coordinator.

---

### 4. `resolve/cmd.py` — `cmd_resolve` (line 48, ~111 LOC)

SKIP. This is a multi-step command handler that validates inputs, loads state, calls resolution, persists, updates the plan, prints output, and writes query. Each step is sequential and labeled. The branching is minimal (`status == "fixed"`, `has_living_plan()`, `purged`). The LOC is high because it orchestrates many steps, not because each step has complex logic.

---

### 5. `review/batch_core.py` — 2 functions

**`_normalize_findings` (line 191, ~96 LOC)**
SKIP. Validation loop over a list of findings from a JSON payload — validates each item, accumulates errors, handles the `impact_scope`/`fix_scope` fallback from `dimension_notes`, then does a priority-preserving trim. The conditional logic at the trim phase is inherently about preserving required dimensions before falling back to order. Clear and purposeful.

**`normalize_batch_result` (line 342, ~87 LOC)**
SKIP. Validates and normalizes a full batch payload: checks keys, iterates assessments, validates each dimension note, handles `abstraction_fitness` sub-axes. This is a validation pipeline — each branch handles a different type error or edge case. Extracting sub-helpers would scatter the contract checks.

**`do_run_batches` (line 409, ~310+ LOC)**

The nested `_report_progress` closure alone is ~120 LOC with an `if event == ...` dispatch. FIX. Five trust modes (`trusted_internal`, `attested_external`, `manual_override`, `findings_only`, with and without provenance) each return immediately. The function reads like a decision table. Converting the `findings_only` section (lines 235–269) into `_build_findings_only_policy_reason(provenance_status, provenance_reason)` would reduce noise, but more importantly: each of the 5 trust-mode branches could be a `_handle_X_mode()` helper returning `(payload, errors)`. ## Group 1: `_print_strict_target_nudge` -- Cross-package import from helpers to command modules

**Finding 1:** `resolve/render.py` imports `_print_strict_target_nudge` from `helpers/score_update.py`
**Finding 2:** `scan/scan_reporting_summary.py` imports `_print_strict_target_nudge` from `helpers/score_update.py`

Both importers are in `desloppify/app/commands/` subdirectories (`resolve/` and `scan/`), while the source is in `desloppify/app/commands/helpers/`. The `helpers/` package exists specifically to provide shared utilities to the other command modules. These cross sub-package boundaries.

- **Classification: FIX** -- `_print_strict_target_nudge` is a shared helper consumed by multiple command packages; it should be renamed to `print_strict_target_nudge` (public API of the helpers package).

---

## Group 2: `_analyze_test_quality`, `_build_test_import_index`, etc. -- Cross-package import between detector packages

**Findings 3-8:** `engine/detectors/test_coverage/detector.py` imports six private functions from `engine/detectors/coverage/mapping.py`

The importer is in `desloppify/engine/detectors/test_coverage/` and the source is in `desloppify/engine/detectors/coverage/`. These are **separate packages** under `engine/detectors/`. The `test_coverage` detector depends heavily on mapping utilities defined in the `coverage` package.

- **Classification: FIX** -- These six functions (`_analyze_test_quality`, `_build_test_import_index`, `_get_test_files_for_prod`, `_import_based_mapping`, `_naming_based_mapping`, `_transitive_coverage`) are the public API of `coverage/mapping.py` as consumed by a sibling detector package. They should be made public (remove `_` prefix) or re-exported through `coverage/__init__.py`.

---

## Group 3: `_phase_coupling` and `_phase_structural` -- Sibling imports within language plugin packages

**Findings 9-10:** `csharp/__init__.py` imports `_phase_coupling`, `_phase_structural` from `csharp/phases.py`
**Findings 11-12:** `dart/__init__.py` imports `_phase_coupling`, `_phase_structural` from `dart/phases.py`
**Findings 13-14:** `gdscript/__init__.py` imports `_phase_coupling`, `_phase_structural` from `gdscript/phases.py`
**Finding 15:** `go/__init__.py` imports `_phase_structural` from `go/phases.py`

Note: The findings describe the source as `_framework/treesitter/phases.py`, but the actual import paths in the code are from each language's own `phases.py` module (e.g., `from desloppify.languages.dart.phases import _phase_coupling`). These are **sibling files within the same package** -- the `__init__.py` assembles the plugin configuration from the adjacent `phases.py`.

- **Classification: SKIP** -- These are same-package sibling imports; `__init__.py` is the natural place to consume private module members from the same package.

---

## Group 4: `_coverage_reduction_warnings` -- Sub-package importing from parent sibling module

**Finding 16:** `scan/reporting/integrity_report.py` imports `_coverage_reduction_warnings` from `scan/scan_reporting_analysis.py`

The importer is in `desloppify/app/commands/scan/reporting/` (a sub-package), importing from `desloppify/app/commands/scan/scan_reporting_analysis.py` (a module in the parent package). This is a nested sub-package reaching up to its parent, which is essentially the same conceptual package.

- **Classification: SKIP** -- The `reporting/` sub-package is part of the `scan/` package; importing a private helper from the parent is acceptable internal plumbing.

---

## Group 5: `_is_agent_environment` and `_print_llm_summary` -- Backward-compatible re-export shim

**Findings 17-18:** `scan/scan_reporting_llm.py` imports `_is_agent_environment` and `_print_llm_summary` from `scan/reporting/agent_context.py`

Looking at the code, `scan_reporting_llm.py` is explicitly a "backward-compatible re-export" shim -- its entire content is importing from the `reporting/` sub-package and re-exporting via `__all__`. The parent package module re-exports from its own child sub-package.

- **Classification: SKIP** -- This is a deliberate backward-compatibility re-export layer within the same package hierarchy.

---

## Group 6: `_unenriched_clusters` -- Re-export through shared.py within triage sub-package

**Finding 19:** `plan/triage_handlers.py` imports `_unenriched_clusters` from `plan/triage/shared.py`

The importer is `desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage_handlers.py` and the source is `desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/shared.py`. The `triage/shared.py` file is itself a re-export hub (it imports from `triage/stage_helpers.py` and re-exports). `triage_handlers.py` sits in `plan/` and imports from `plan/triage/`, a child sub-package.

- **Classification: SKIP** -- Parent module importing from its own child sub-package's shared exports; this is normal internal package structure.

   194→def _detect_ast_smells(filepath: str, content: str, smell_counts: dict[str, list]):
   195→    """Detect AST-based code smells using registry-driven collector dispatch."""
   196→    try:

   204→        node
   205→        for node in all_nodes
   206→        if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef)
   207→    )
   208→
   209→    for spec in NODE_DETECTORS:
   210→        matches: list[SmellMatch] = []
   211→        for fn_node in fn_nodes:
   212→            matches.extend(spec.collect(filepath, fn_node, tree))
   213→        merge_smell_matches(smell_counts, spec.smell_id, matches)
   214→
   215→    for spec in TREE_DETECTORS:
   216→        matches = spec.collect(filepath, tree, all_nodes)
   217→        merge_smell_matches(smell_counts, spec.smell_id, matches)
   218→

   369→    if not lang:

   371→
   372→    lang_options = resolve_lang_runtime_options(args, lang)
   373→    lang_settings = resolve_lang_settings(config, lang)
   374→    runtime_lang = make_lang_run(
   375→        lang,
   376→        overrides=LangRunOverrides(
   377→            review_cache=state.get("review_cache", {}),
   378→            review_max_age_days=config.get("review_max_age_days", 30),
   379→            runtime_settings=lang_settings,

   382→            props_threshold_override=config.get("props_threshold", 0),
   383→        ),
   384→    )
   385→
   386→    lang_capabilities = _state_lang_capabilities(state)
   387→    lang_capabilities[runtime_lang.name] = {
   388→        "fixers": sorted(runtime_lang.fixers.keys()),
   389→        "typecheck_cmd": runtime_lang.typecheck_cmd,
   390→    }
   391→    return runtime_lang

   394→def _reset_subjective_assessments_for_scan_reset(
   395→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   396→    *,
   397→    lang_name: str | None = None,
   398→) -> int:
   399→    """Reset known subjective dimensions to 0 so the next scan starts fresh."""
   400→    assessments = _state_subjective_assessments(state)
   401→
   402→    reset_keys = {
   403→        key.strip()
   404→        for key in assessments
   405→        if isinstance(key, str) and key.strip()
   406→    }
   407→    reset_keys.update(_subjective_reset_dimensions(lang_name=lang_name))
   408→
   409→    now = state_mod.utc_now()
   410→    for key in sorted(reset_keys):
   411→        payload = assessments.get(key)
   412→        if isinstance(payload, dict):
   413→            payload["score"] = 0.0
   414→            payload["source"] = "scan_reset_subjective"
   415→            payload["assessed_at"] = now
   416→            payload["reset_by"] = "scan_reset_subjective"
   417→            payload["placeholder"] = True
   418→            payload.pop("integrity_penalty", None)
   419→            payload.pop("components", None)
   420→            payload.pop("component_scores", None)
   421→            continue
   422→        assessments[key] = {
   423→            "score": 0.0,
   424→            "source": "scan_reset_subjective",
   425→            "assessed_at": now,
   426→            "reset_by": "scan_reset_subjective",
   427→            "placeholder": True,
   428→        }
   429→    return len(reset_keys)

   432→def _expire_provisional_manual_override_assessments(
   433→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   434→) -> int:
   435→    """Expire provisional manual-override assessments at scan start."""
   436→    assessments = _state_subjective_assessments(state)
   437→
   438→    now = state_mod.utc_now()
   439→    expired = 0
   440→    for payload in assessments.values():
   441→        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
   442→            continue
   443→        if payload.get("provisional_override") is not True:
   444→            continue
   445→        payload["score"] = 0.0
   446→        payload["source"] = "manual_override_expired"
   447→        payload["assessed_at"] = now
   448→        payload["reset_by"] = "manual_override_expired"
   449→        payload["placeholder"] = True
   450→        payload.pop("provisional_override", None)
   451→        payload.pop("provisional_until_scan", None)
   452→        payload.pop("integrity_penalty", None)
   453→        payload.pop("components", None)
   454→        payload.pop("component_scores", None)
   455→        expired += 1
   456→    return expired

   461→    runtime = command_runtime(args)

   464→    state_mod.ensure_state_defaults(state)

   473→        reset_subjective_count = _reset_subjective_assessments_for_scan_reset(
   474→            state,

   477→
   478→    include_slow = not getattr(args, "skip_slow", False)
   479→    profile = _resolve_scan_profile(getattr(args, "profile", None), lang_config)
   480→    effective_include_slow = _effective_include_slow(include_slow, profile)
   481→
   482→    lang = _configure_lang_runtime(args, config, state, lang_config)
   483→    coverage_warnings = _seed_runtime_coverage_warnings(lang)

   486→

   504→def _augment_with_stale_exclusion_findings(
   505→    findings: list[dict[str, Any]],
   506→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   507→) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   508→    """Append stale exclude findings when excluded dirs are unreferenced."""
   509→    extra_exclusions = get_exclusions()
   510→    if not (extra_exclusions and runtime.lang and runtime.lang.file_finder):
   511→        return findings
   512→
   513→    scanned_files = runtime.lang.file_finder(runtime.path)
   514→    stale = _audit_excluded_dirs(
   515→        extra_exclusions, scanned_files, PROJECT_ROOT
   516→    )
   517→    if not stale:
   518→        return findings
   519→
   520→    augmented = list(findings)
   521→    augmented.extend(stale)
   522→    for stale_finding in stale:
   523→        print(colorize(f"  ℹ {stale_finding['summary']}", "dim"))
   524→    return augmented

   543→def run_scan_generation(
   544→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   545→) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], dict[str, object], dict[str, object] | None]:
   546→    """Run detector pipeline and return findings, potentials, and codebase metrics."""
   547→    enable_file_cache()
   548→    enable_parse_cache()
   549→    try:
   550→        findings, potentials = plan_mod.generate_findings(
   551→            runtime.path,
   552→            lang=runtime.lang,
   553→            options=PlanScanOptions(
   554→                include_slow=runtime.effective_include_slow,
   555→                zone_overrides=runtime.zone_overrides,
   556→                profile=runtime.profile,
   557→            ),
   558→        )
   559→    finally:
   560→        disable_parse_cache()
   561→        disable_file_cache()
   562→
   563→    codebase_metrics = _collect_codebase_metrics(runtime.lang, runtime.path)
   564→    _warn_explicit_lang_with_no_files(
   565→        runtime.args, runtime.lang, runtime.path, codebase_metrics
   566→    )
   567→    findings = _augment_with_stale_exclusion_findings(findings, runtime)
   568→    decay_scans = _coerce_int(
   569→        runtime.config.get("wontfix_decay_scans"),
   570→        default=_WONTFIX_DECAY_SCANS_DEFAULT,
   571→    )
   572→    findings, monitored_wontfix = _augment_with_stale_wontfix_findings(
   573→        findings,
   574→        runtime,
   575→        decay_scans=max(decay_scans, 0),
   576→    )
   577→    potentials["stale_wontfix"] = monitored_wontfix
   578→    return findings, potentials, codebase_metrics
   579→
   580→
   581→def merge_scan_results(
   582→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   583→    findings: list[dict[str, Any]],
   584→    potentials: dict[str, object],
   585→    codebase_metrics: dict[str, object] | None,
   586→) -> ScanMergeResult:
   587→    """Merge findings into persistent state and return diff + previous score snapshot."""
   588→    scan_path_rel = rel(str(runtime.path))
   589→    prev_scan_path = runtime.state.get("scan_path")
   590→    path_changed = prev_scan_path is not None and prev_scan_path != scan_path_rel
   591→
   592→    if not path_changed:
   593→        prev = state_mod.score_snapshot(runtime.state)
   594→    else:
   595→        prev = state_mod.ScoreSnapshot(None, None, None, None)
   596→    prev_dim_scores = (
   597→        runtime.state.get("dimension_scores", {}) if not path_changed else {}
   598→    )
   599→
   600→    if runtime.lang and runtime.lang.zone_map is not None:
   601→        runtime.state["zone_distribution"] = runtime.lang.zone_map.counts()
   602→    _persist_scan_coverage(runtime.state, runtime.lang)
   603→
   604→    target_score = target_strict_score_from_config(runtime.config, fallback=95.0)
   605→
   606→    diff = state_mod.merge_scan(
   607→        runtime.state,
   608→        findings,
   609→        options=state_mod.MergeScanOptions(
   610→            lang=runtime.lang.name if runtime.lang else None,
   611→            scan_path=scan_path_rel,
   612→            force_resolve=getattr(runtime.args, "force_resolve", False),
   613→            exclude=get_exclusions(),
   614→            potentials=potentials,
   615→            codebase_metrics=codebase_metrics,
   616→            include_slow=runtime.effective_include_slow,
   617→            ignore=runtime.config.get("ignore", []),
   618→            subjective_integrity_target=target_score,
   619→        ),
   620→    )
   621→
   622→    issues_mod.expire_stale_holistic(
   623→        runtime.state, runtime.config.get("holistic_max_age_days", 30)
   624→    )
   625→    state_mod.save_state(
   626→        runtime.state,
   627→        runtime.state_path,
   628→        subjective_integrity_target=target_score,
   629→    )
   630→
   631→    _clear_needs_rescan_flag(runtime.config)
   632→    _reconcile_plan_post_scan(runtime)
   633→
   634→    return ScanMergeResult(
   635→        diff=diff,
   636→        prev_overall=prev.overall,
   637→        prev_objective=prev.objective,
   638→        prev_strict=prev.strict,
   639→        prev_verified=prev.verified,
   640→        prev_dim_scores=prev_dim_scores,
   641→    )
   642→
   643→
   644→def resolve_noise_snapshot(
   645→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   646→    config: dict[str, object],
   647→) -> ScanNoiseSnapshot:
   648→    """Resolve noise budget settings and hidden finding counters."""
   649→    noise_budget, global_noise_budget, budget_warning = (
   650→        state_mod.resolve_finding_noise_settings(config)
   651→    )
   652→    findings_by_id = _state_findings(state)
   653→    open_findings = [
   654→        finding
   655→        for finding in state_mod.path_scoped_findings(
   656→            findings_by_id, state.get("scan_path")
   657→        ).values()
   658→        if finding.get("status") == "open"
   659→    ]
   660→    _, hidden_by_detector = state_mod.apply_finding_noise_budget(
   661→        open_findings,
   662→        budget=noise_budget,
   663→        global_budget=global_noise_budget,
   664→    )
   665→
   666→    return ScanNoiseSnapshot(
   667→        noise_budget=noise_budget,
   668→        global_noise_budget=global_noise_budget,
   669→        budget_warning=budget_warning,
   670→        hidden_by_detector=hidden_by_detector,
   671→        hidden_total=sum(hidden_by_detector.values()),
   672→    )
   673→
   674→
   675→def persist_reminder_history(
   676→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   677→    narrative: dict[str, object],
   678→) -> None:
   679→    """Persist reminder history emitted by narrative computation."""
   680→    if not (narrative and "reminder_history" in narrative):
   681→        return
   682→
   683→    runtime.state["reminder_history"] = narrative["reminder_history"]
   684→    target_score = target_strict_score_from_config(runtime.config, fallback=95.0)
   685→    state_mod.save_state(
   686→        runtime.state,
   687→        runtime.state_path,
   688→        subjective_integrity_target=target_score,
   689→    )

   171→        fid = f"{SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX}{slugify(dim_key)}"
   172→        if fid not in stale_ids and fid not in unscored_ids:
   173→            under_target.add(fid)
   174→    return under_target
   175→
   176→
   177→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   178→# Promoted-aware insertion helper
   179→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   180→
   181→def _after_promoted(order: list[str], plan: PlanModel) -> int:
   182→    """Return the insertion index just after the last promoted item in *order*.
   183→
   184→    When no promoted items are present (or none are in *order*), returns 0
   185→    so callers fall back to existing front-of-queue behavior.
   186→    """
   187→    promoted = set(plan.get("promoted_ids", []))
   188→    if not promoted:
   189→        return 0
   190→    last_idx = -1
   191→    for i, fid in enumerate(order):
   192→        if fid in promoted:
   193→            last_idx = i
   194→    return last_idx + 1 if last_idx >= 0 else 0
   195→
   196→
   197→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   198→# Unscored dimension sync (front of queue, unconditional)
   199→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   200→
   201→def sync_unscored_dimensions(
   202→    plan: PlanModel,
   203→    state: StateModel,
   204→) -> UnscoredDimensionSyncResult:
   205→    """Keep the plan queue in sync with unscored (placeholder) subjective dimensions.
   206→
   207→    1. **Prune** — remove ``subjective::*`` IDs from ``queue_order`` that are
   208→       no longer unscored AND not stale (avoids pruning stale IDs — that is
   209→       ``sync_stale_dimensions``' responsibility).
   210→    2. **Inject** — unconditionally prepend currently-unscored IDs to the
   211→       *front* of ``queue_order`` so initial reviews are the first priority.
   212→    """
   213→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   214→    result = UnscoredDimensionSyncResult()
   215→    unscored_ids = current_unscored_ids(state)
   216→    stale_ids = _current_stale_ids(state)
   217→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   218→
   219→    # --- Cleanup: prune subjective IDs that are no longer unscored --------
   220→    # Only prune IDs that are neither unscored nor stale (stale sync owns those).
   221→    to_remove: list[str] = [
   222→        fid for fid in order
   223→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX)
   224→        and fid not in unscored_ids
   225→        and fid not in stale_ids
   226→    ]
   227→    for fid in to_remove:
   228→        order.remove(fid)
   229→        result.pruned.append(fid)
   230→
   231→    # --- Inject: prepend unscored IDs after any promoted items -------------
   232→    existing = set(order)
   233→    insert_at = _after_promoted(order, plan)
   234→    for uid in reversed(sorted(unscored_ids)):
   235→        if uid not in existing:
   236→            order.insert(insert_at, uid)
   237→            result.injected.append(uid)
   238→
   239→    return result
   240→
   241→
   242→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   243→# Stale dimension sync (back of queue, conditional)
   244→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   245→
   246→def sync_stale_dimensions(
   247→    plan: PlanModel,
   248→    state: StateModel,
   249→    *,
   250→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   251→) -> StaleDimensionSyncResult:
   252→    """Keep the plan queue in sync with stale subjective dimensions.
   253→
   254→    1. Remove any ``subjective::*`` IDs from ``queue_order`` that are no
   255→       longer stale and not unscored (avoids pruning IDs owned by
   256→       ``sync_unscored_dimensions``).
   257→    2. If no objective items remain after cleanup, inject all currently-stale
   258→       dimension IDs so the plan surfaces them as actionable work.
   259→    """
   260→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   261→    result = StaleDimensionSyncResult()
   262→    stale_ids = _current_stale_ids(state)
   263→    unscored_ids = current_unscored_ids(state)
   264→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   265→
   266→    # --- Cleanup: prune resolved subjective IDs --------------------------
   267→    # Only prune IDs that are neither stale nor unscored.
   268→    to_remove: list[str] = [
   269→        fid for fid in order
   270→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX)
   271→        and fid not in stale_ids
   272→        and fid not in unscored_ids
   273→    ]
   274→    for fid in to_remove:
   275→        order.remove(fid)
   276→        result.pruned.append(fid)
   277→
   278→    # --- Inject: populate when no objective items remain -----------------
   279→    if policy is not None:
   280→        has_real_items = policy.has_objective_backlog
   281→    else:
   282→        has_real_items = any(
   283→            f.get("status") == "open"
   284→            and f.get("detector") not in NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS
   285→            and not f.get("suppressed")
   286→            for f in state.get("findings", {}).values()
   287→        )
   288→    if not has_real_items and stale_ids:
   289→        existing = set(order)
   290→        for sid in sorted(stale_ids):
   291→            if sid not in existing:
   292→                order.append(sid)
   293→                result.injected.append(sid)
   294→
   295→    return result
   296→
   297→
   298→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   299→# Triage snapshot hash + sync
   300→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   301→
   302→def review_finding_snapshot_hash(state: StateModel) -> str:
   303→    """Hash open review finding IDs to detect changes.
   304→
   305→    Returns empty string when there are no open review findings.
   306→    """
   307→    findings = state.get("findings", {})
   308→    review_ids = sorted(
   309→        fid for fid, f in findings.items()
   310→        if f.get("status") == "open"
   311→        and f.get("detector") in ("review", "concerns")
   312→    )
   313→    if not review_ids:
   314→        return ""
   315→    return hashlib.sha256("|".join(review_ids).encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
   316→
   317→
   318→@dataclass
   319→class TriageSyncResult:
   320→    """What changed during a triage sync."""
   321→
   322→    injected: bool = False
   323→    pruned: bool = False
   324→
   325→    @property
   326→    def changes(self) -> int:
   327→        return int(self.injected) + int(self.pruned)
   328→
   329→
   330→def sync_triage_needed(
   331→    plan: PlanModel,
   332→    state: StateModel,
   333→) -> TriageSyncResult:
   334→    """Inject 4 triage stage IDs at front of queue when review findings change.
   335→
   336→    Only injects stages not already confirmed in ``epic_triage_meta``.
   337→    Never auto-prunes — only explicit completion removes them.
   338→
   339→    When findings are *resolved* (current IDs are a subset of previously
   340→    triaged IDs), the snapshot hash is updated silently — no re-triage
   341→    is needed since the user is working through the plan.
   342→    """
   343→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   344→    result = TriageSyncResult()
   345→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   346→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   347→    confirmed = set(meta.get("triage_stages", {}).keys())
   348→
   349→    # Check if any triage stage is already in queue
   350→    already_present = any(sid in order for sid in TRIAGE_IDS)
   351→
   352→    current_hash = review_finding_snapshot_hash(state)
   353→    last_hash = meta.get("finding_snapshot_hash", "")
   354→
   355→    if current_hash and current_hash != last_hash and not already_present:
   356→        # Distinguish "new findings appeared" from "findings were resolved".
   357→        # Only re-triage when genuinely new findings exist.
   358→        findings = state.get("findings", {})
   359→        current_review_ids = {
   360→            fid for fid, f in findings.items()
   361→            if f.get("status") == "open"
   362→            and f.get("detector") in ("review", "concerns")
   363→        }
   364→        triaged_ids = set(meta.get("triaged_ids", []))
   365→        new_since_triage = current_review_ids - triaged_ids
   366→
   367→        if new_since_triage:
   368→            # New review findings appeared — re-triage needed
   369→            insert_at = _after_promoted(order, plan)
   370→            stage_names = ("observe", "reflect", "organize", "commit")
   371→            existing = set(order)
   372→            injected_count = 0
   373→            for sid, name in zip(TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS, stage_names):
   374→                if name not in confirmed and sid not in existing:
   375→                    order.insert(insert_at + injected_count, sid)
   376→                    injected_count += 1
   377→            if injected_count:
   378→                result.injected = True
   379→        else:
   380→            # Only resolved findings changed the hash — update silently
   381→            meta["finding_snapshot_hash"] = current_hash
   382→            plan["epic_triage_meta"] = meta
   383→
   384→    return result
   385→
   386→
   387→@dataclass
   388→class CreatePlanSyncResult:
   389→    """What changed during a create-plan sync."""
   390→
   391→    injected: bool = False
   392→
   393→    @property
   394→    def changes(self) -> int:
   395→        return int(self.injected)
   396→
   397→
   398→def sync_create_plan_needed(
   399→    plan: PlanModel,
   400→    state: StateModel,
   401→    *,
   402→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   403→) -> CreatePlanSyncResult:
   404→    """Inject ``workflow::create-plan`` when reviews complete + objective backlog exists.
   405→
   406→    Only injects when:
   407→    - No unscored (placeholder) subjective dimensions remain
   408→    - At least one objective finding exists
   409→    - ``workflow::create-plan`` is not already in the queue
   410→    - No triage stages are pending
   411→    """
   412→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   413→    result = CreatePlanSyncResult()
   414→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   415→
   416→    if WORKFLOW_CREATE_PLAN_ID in order:
   417→        return result
   418→
   419→    # Don't inject if triage stages are pending
   420→    if any(sid in order for sid in TRIAGE_IDS):
   421→        return result
   422→
   423→    # Check that no unscored dimensions remain
   424→    if policy is not None:
   425→        if policy.unscored_ids:
   426→            return result
   427→        has_objective = policy.has_objective_backlog
   428→    else:
   429→        unscored = current_unscored_ids(state)
   430→        if unscored:
   431→            return result
   432→        findings = state.get("findings", {})
   433→        has_objective = any(
   434→            f.get("status") == "open"
   435→            and f.get("detector") not in NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS
   436→            for f in findings.values()
   437→        )
   438→    if not has_objective:
   439→        return result
   440→
   441→    # Insert after any subjective items, before findings
   442→    insert_at = 0
   443→    for i, fid in enumerate(order):
   444→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX) or fid.startswith(TRIAGE_PREFIX):
   445→            insert_at = i + 1
   446→    order.insert(insert_at, WORKFLOW_CREATE_PLAN_ID)
   447→    result.injected = True
   448→    return result
   449→
   450→
   451→def compute_new_finding_ids(plan: PlanModel, state: StateModel) -> set[str]:
   452→    """Return the set of open review/concerns finding IDs added since last triage.
   453→
   454→    Returns an empty set when no prior triage has recorded ``triaged_ids``.
   455→    """
   456→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   457→    triaged = set(meta.get("triaged_ids", meta.get("synthesized_ids", [])))
   458→    current = {
   459→        fid for fid, f in state.get("findings", {}).items()
   460→        if f.get("status") == "open" and f.get("detector") in ("review", "concerns")
   461→    }
   462→    return current - triaged if triaged else set()
   463→
   464→
   465→def is_triage_stale(plan: PlanModel, state: StateModel) -> bool:
   466→    """Side-effect-free check: is triage needed?
   467→
   468→    Returns True when any ``triage::*`` stage ID is in the queue OR
   469→    genuinely *new* review findings appeared since the last triage.
   470→
   471→    When findings are merely resolved (current IDs are a subset of
   472→    previously triaged IDs), triage is NOT stale — the user is working
   473→    through the plan.
   474→    """
   475→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   476→    order = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
   477→    if order & TRIAGE_IDS:
   478→        return True
   479→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   480→    last_hash = meta.get("finding_snapshot_hash", "")
   481→    if not last_hash:
   482→        return False
   483→    current_hash = review_finding_snapshot_hash(state)
   484→    if not current_hash or current_hash == last_hash:
   485→        return False
   486→    # Hash changed — check if new findings appeared or only resolutions
   487→    findings = state.get("findings", {})
   488→    current_review_ids = {
   489→        fid for fid, f in findings.items()
   490→        if f.get("status") == "open"
   491→        and f.get("detector") in ("review", "concerns")
   492→    }
   493→    triaged_ids = set(meta.get("triaged_ids", []))
   494→    new_since_triage = current_review_ids - triaged_ids
   495→    return bool(new_since_triage)
   496→
   497→
   498→
   499→__all__ = [
   500→    "NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS",
   501→    "SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX",
   502→    "TRIAGE_ID",
   503→    "TRIAGE_IDS",
   504→    "TRIAGE_PREFIX",
   505→    "TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS",
   506→    "SYNTHETIC_PREFIXES",
   507→    "WORKFLOW_CREATE_PLAN_ID",
   508→    "WORKFLOW_PREFIX",
   509→    "CreatePlanSyncResult",

   107→def _prune_old_superseded(plan: PlanModel, now_dt: datetime) -> list[str]:
   108→    """Remove superseded entries older than TTL. Returns pruned IDs."""
   109→    superseded = plan.get("superseded", {})
   110→    cutoff = now_dt - timedelta(days=SUPERSEDED_TTL_DAYS)
   111→    to_prune: list[str] = []
   112→
   113→    for fid, entry in superseded.items():
   114→        ts = entry.get("superseded_at", "")
   115→        try:
   116→            entry_dt = datetime.fromisoformat(ts)
   117→            if entry_dt.tzinfo is None:
   118→                entry_dt = entry_dt.replace(tzinfo=UTC)
   119→            if entry_dt < cutoff:
   120→                to_prune.append(fid)
   121→        except (ValueError, TypeError):
   122→            to_prune.append(fid)
   123→
   124→    for fid in to_prune:
   125→        superseded.pop(fid, None)
   126→        # Also clean up stale overrides
   127→        plan.get("overrides", {}).pop(fid, None)
   128→
   129→    return to_prune

   132→def reconcile_plan_after_scan(
   133→    plan: PlanModel,
   134→    state: StateModel,
   135→) -> ReconcileResult:
   136→    """Reconcile plan against current state after a scan.
   137→
   138→    Finds IDs referenced in the plan that no longer exist or are no longer
   139→    open, moves them to superseded, and prunes old superseded entries.
   140→    """
   141→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   142→    result = ReconcileResult()
   143→    now = utc_now()
   144→    now_dt = datetime.now(UTC)
   145→
   146→    # Collect all finding IDs referenced by the plan
   147→    referenced_ids: set[str] = set()
   148→    referenced_ids.update(plan.get("queue_order", []))
   149→    referenced_ids.update(plan.get("skipped", {}).keys())
   150→    for override_id in plan.get("overrides", {}):
   151→        referenced_ids.add(override_id)
   152→    for cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).values():
   153→        referenced_ids.update(cluster.get("finding_ids", []))
   154→
   155→    # Exclude already-superseded IDs and synthetic IDs (managed by stale_dimensions)
   156→    already_superseded = set(plan.get("superseded", {}).keys())
   157→    referenced_ids -= already_superseded
   158→    referenced_ids = {
   159→        fid for fid in referenced_ids
   160→        if not any(fid.startswith(prefix) for prefix in SYNTHETIC_PREFIXES)
   161→    }
   162→
   163→    # Check each referenced ID
   164→    for fid in sorted(referenced_ids):
   165→        if not _is_finding_alive(state, fid):
   166→            if _supersede_id(plan, state, fid, now):
   167→                result.superseded.append(fid)
   168→                result.changes += 1
   169→
   170→    # Reconcile epic clusters: remove dead findings, delete empty epics
   171→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   172→    epic_names_to_delete: list[str] = []
   173→    for name, cluster in list(clusters.items()):
   174→        if not name.startswith(EPIC_PREFIX):
   175→            continue
   176→        finding_ids = cluster.get("finding_ids", [])
   177→        alive_ids = [fid for fid in finding_ids if _is_finding_alive(state, fid)]
   178→        if alive_ids != finding_ids:
   179→            cluster["finding_ids"] = alive_ids
   180→            result.changes += 1
   181→        if not alive_ids:
   182→            epic_names_to_delete.append(name)
   183→    for name in epic_names_to_delete:
   184→        clusters.pop(name, None)
   185→        result.changes += 1
   186→
   187→    # Resurface stale temporary skips
   188→    scan_count = state.get("scan_count", 0)
   189→    from desloppify.engine._plan.operations import resurface_stale_skips
   190→
   191→    resurfaced = resurface_stale_skips(plan, scan_count)
   192→    if resurfaced:
   193→        result.resurfaced = resurfaced
   194→        result.changes += len(resurfaced)
   195→
   196→    # Prune old superseded entries
   197→    pruned = _prune_old_superseded(plan, now_dt)
   198→    result.pruned = pruned
   199→    result.changes += len(pruned)
   200→
   201→    # Log reconciliation if any changes were made
   202→    if result.changes > 0:
   203→        from desloppify.engine._plan.operations import append_log_entry
   204→
   205→        append_log_entry(
   206→            plan,
   207→            "reconcile",
   208→            finding_ids=result.superseded,
   209→            actor="system",
   210→            detail={
   211→                "superseded_count": len(result.superseded),
   212→                "pruned_count": len(result.pruned),
   213→                "resurfaced_count": len(result.resurfaced),
   214→            },
   215→        )
   216→
   217→    return result

   220→@dataclass
   221→class ReviewImportSyncResult:
   222→    """Summary of plan changes after a review import."""
   223→
   224→    new_ids: set[str]
   225→    added_to_queue: list[str]
   226→    triage_injected: bool
   227→
   228→
   229→def sync_plan_after_review_import(
   230→    plan: PlanModel,
   231→    state: StateModel,
   232→) -> ReviewImportSyncResult | None:
   233→    """Sync plan queue after review import. Pure engine function — no I/O.
   234→
   235→    Appends new finding IDs to queue_order and injects triage stages
   236→    if needed. Returns None when there are no new findings to sync.
   237→    """
   238→    from desloppify.engine._plan.stale_dimensions import (
   239→        compute_new_finding_ids,
   240→        sync_triage_needed,
   241→    )
   242→
   243→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   244→    new_ids = compute_new_finding_ids(plan, state)
   245→    if not new_ids:
   246→        return None
   247→
   248→    # Add new finding IDs to end of queue_order so they have position
   249→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   250→    existing = set(order)
   251→    added: list[str] = []
   252→    for fid in sorted(new_ids):
   253→        if fid not in existing:
   254→            order.append(fid)
   255→            added.append(fid)
   256→
   257→    # Inject triage stages if needed
   258→    triage_result = sync_triage_needed(plan, state)
   259→    triage_injected = bool(
   260→        triage_result and getattr(triage_result, "injected", False)
   261→    )
   262→
   263→    return ReviewImportSyncResult(
   264→        new_ids=new_ids,
   265→        added_to_queue=added,
   266→        triage_injected=triage_injected,
   267→    )
   268→
   269→
   270→__all__ = [
   271→    "ReconcileResult",
   272→    "ReviewImportSyncResult",
   273→    "reconcile_plan_after_scan",
   274→    "sync_plan_after_review_import",
   275→]

1→"""Unified subjective-visibility policy.
     2→
     3→A single frozen dataclass computed once per operation replaces the scattered
     4→``has_objective_items`` / ``objective_count`` computations in
     5→``stale_dimensions``, ``auto_cluster``, and ``_work_queue/core``.
     6→"""
     7→
     8→from __future__ import annotations
     9→
    10→from dataclasses import dataclass
    11→
    12→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import StateModel
    13→
    14→# Detectors whose findings are NOT objective mechanical work.
    15→# Canonical definition — re-exported by stale_dimensions for back-compat.
    16→NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS: frozenset[str] = frozenset({
    17→    "review", "concerns", "subjective_review", "subjective_assessment",
    18→})
    19→
    20→
    21→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    22→class SubjectiveVisibility:
    23→    """Immutable snapshot of the subjective-vs-objective balance."""
    24→
    25→    has_objective_backlog: bool  # any open non-subjective findings?
    26→    objective_count: int  # how many
    27→    unscored_ids: frozenset[str]  # subjective::* IDs needing initial review
    28→    stale_ids: frozenset[str]  # subjective::* IDs needing re-review
    29→    under_target_ids: frozenset[str]  # below target, not stale/unscored
    30→
    31→    def should_surface(self, item: dict) -> bool:
    32→        """Should this subjective queue item appear in the work queue?
    33→
    34→        Unscored (initial_review) -> always.  All others -> only when drained.
    35→        """
    36→        if item.get("initial_review"):
    37→            return True
    38→        return not self.has_objective_backlog
    39→
    40→    def should_inject_to_plan(self, fid: str) -> bool:
    41→        """Should this subjective ID be injected into plan queue_order?"""
    42→        if fid in self.unscored_ids:
    43→            return True  # unconditional
    44→        if fid in self.stale_ids:
    45→            return not self.has_objective_backlog
    46→        if fid in self.under_target_ids:
    47→            return not self.has_objective_backlog
    48→        return False
    49→
    50→    def should_evict_from_plan(self, fid: str) -> bool:
    51→        """Should this subjective ID be removed from plan queue_order?"""
    52→        if fid in self.unscored_ids:
    53→            return False  # never evict unscored
    54→        if fid in self.stale_ids or fid in self.under_target_ids:
    55→            return self.has_objective_backlog
    56→        return False
    57→
    58→    @property
    59→    def backlog_blocks_rerun(self) -> bool:
    60→        """Preflight: should reruns be blocked?"""
    61→        return self.has_objective_backlog
    62→
    63→
    64→def _is_evidence_only(finding: dict) -> bool:
    65→    """Return True if the finding is below its detector's standalone threshold."""
    66→    from desloppify.core.registry import DETECTORS
    67→    from desloppify.engine.planning.common import CONFIDENCE_ORDER
    68→
    69→    detector = finding.get("detector", "")
    70→    meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
    71→    if meta and meta.standalone_threshold:
    72→        threshold_rank = CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(meta.standalone_threshold, 9)
    73→        finding_rank = CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(finding.get("confidence", "low"), 9)
    74→        if finding_rank > threshold_rank:
    75→            return True
    76→    return False
    77→
    78→
    79→def compute_subjective_visibility(
    80→    state: StateModel,
    81→    *,
    82→    target_strict: float = 95.0,
    83→) -> SubjectiveVisibility:
    84→    """Build the policy snapshot from current state.
    85→
    86→    Imports building-block helpers from ``stale_dimensions`` so the
    87→    source-of-truth logic stays in one place.
    88→    """
    89→    from desloppify.engine._plan.stale_dimensions import (
    90→        _current_stale_ids,
    91→        current_under_target_ids,
    92→        current_unscored_ids,
    93→    )
    94→
    95→    findings = state.get("findings", {})
    96→
    97→    # Count open, non-suppressed, objective findings.
    98→    # Evidence-only findings (below standalone confidence threshold) are
    99→    # excluded — they still affect scores but are not actionable queue items.
   100→    objective_count = sum(
   101→        1
   102→        for f in findings.values()
   103→        if f.get("status") == "open"
   104→        and f.get("detector") not in NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS
   105→        and not f.get("suppressed")
   106→        and not _is_evidence_only(f)
   107→    )
   108→
   109→    unscored = current_unscored_ids(state)
   110→    stale = _current_stale_ids(state)
   111→    under_target = current_under_target_ids(state, target_strict=target_strict)
   112→
   113→    return SubjectiveVisibility(
   114→        has_objective_backlog=objective_count > 0,
   115→        objective_count=objective_count,
   116→        unscored_ids=frozenset(unscored),
   117→        stale_ids=frozenset(stale),
   118→        under_target_ids=frozenset(under_target),
   119→    )
   120→
   121→
   122→__all__ = [
   123→    "NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS",
   124→    "SubjectiveVisibility",
   125→    "compute_subjective_visibility",
   126→]
   127→

    34→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
